commits.pr_title: [CI][AMD] Move 17 test groups from MI300 to MI355 and test large DeepSeek/Nemotron evals on AITER
commits.pr_body:
- Move 14 single-GPU groups from `mi300_1` to `mi355_dpx`, and LM Eval Large Models / ROCm Harness from `mi300_8` to `mi355_8` (`test-amd.yaml` + `test_areas` mirrors)
- Move LM Eval KV-Offload Large (DeepSeek-V4-Flash) from `mi300_4` to `mi355_4`
- Drop the MI300 copies whose MI355 twin already exists: Extended Pooling, Multimodal Extended Generation 1 / Extended Pooling, LM Eval Large Models
- Retire the MI300 DeepSeek R1 / V3.2 evals that ran on `TRITON_ATTN` (`models-mi3xx.txt`, `*_MI325.yaml`). Both models already run on MI355 with `ROCM_AITER_MLA(_SPARSE)` and AITER MoE
- Nemotron 3 Super (MI355): use `ROCM_AITER_FA` attention
- V1 E2E Hybrid Chunked Prefill: drop the stale `num_gpus: 4` (the test is TP1, and the mirror already used one GPU)

This is a subset of #60480, split out so these groups move first. DeepSeek R1, V3.2, V4 and Nemotron 3 Super should be gated on AITER on MI355 instead of Triton on MI300. R1, V3.2 and V4 already resolve to AITER on MI355, so for them this PR only removes the MI300 Triton runs and moves the V4 KV-offload eval. Nemotron 3 Super can only switch attention: AITER MoE rejects its non-gated ReLU² experts (`kernel does not support no act_and_mul MLP layer`), and there is no AITER Mamba backend. With `ROCM_AITER_FA`, the CI eval passes 10/10 for each Nemotron config on MI355 (TP4), and accuracy matches the default `ROCM_ATTN`:

| GSM8K, 10 runs | `ROCM_ATTN` (current) | `ROCM_AITER_FA` (this PR) |

| Nemotron-3-Super-FP8 | 0.9329 median (0.9295–0.9356) | 0.9325 median (0.9265–0.9409) |
| Nemotron-3-Super-BF16 | 0.9352 median (0.9325–0.9393) | 0.9352 median (0.9318–0.9409) |

The DeepSeek-V4-Flash KV-offload eval passes on MI355 (0.96–0.98 vs a 0.90 threshold).

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Model] Honor quantization config in Inkling MTP
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Allow Inkling MTP to use the saved quantization config for its input projections and decoder blocks, including per-layer exclusions. This enables serving quantized MTP layers.

## Claims

Honor quantization targets/exclusions and load projection scales on NVIDIA and AMD, without scheme-specific branches.

## Validation

- 15 tests and pre-commit pass; six new regression cases fail on baseline.
- Full-size MTP meta check loads all 136 required parameters with corrected metadata; original metadata fails.
- Tiny H100 BF16/FP8/mixed runs succeed. FP8/mixed match target-only on 8/8 prompts; BF16 behavior is unchanged from baseline.

Limitations: the tiny draft is untrained (zero FP8/mixed acceptance), and GPU tests reused compiled artifacts. Full-model inference/quality, ROCm and multi-GPU remain untested. Meta checks cover MTP construction and shape loading only.

## Details

**Metadata required:** released Inkling-NVFP4 has BF16 MTP weights. Append `model.mtp.*` to `quantization.exclude_modules` in `hf_quant_config.json` before using this change. That metadata correction is not yet published.

Distinct from #60666 (checkpoint renaming) and #48506 (other MTP architectures).

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm][GLM-5.2] Stop forcing skip_final_all_reduce on AMD DSA model path
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`vllm/models/deepseek_v32/amd/model.py` (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.2 on ROCm) forces `skip_final_all_reduce = True`. With a reducing combine (MoRI, DeepEP) `MoERunner` asserts:

```
AssertionError: skip_final_all_reduce requires an un-reduced fused output
```

## Changes

The MoE output is summed over TP in the next `fused_allreduce_rms_norm`.

- `skip_final_all_reduce` only for non-reducing combines (no all2all, `allgather_reducescatter`).
- If the combine reduces or the layer is sequence-parallel, the output is complete on every TP rank: zero it on TP rank > 0.

## Test Plan

ROCm image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly`, MI350X, GLM-5.2-FP8.

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MLA=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 \
       VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_RMSNORM=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0 \
       VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP8BMM=false
```

DP8/EP8/TP1, MoRI: MoRIIO 1P1D (one prefill node, one decode node), with [#58585](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58585).

```bash
# prefill: --all2all-backend mori_high_throughput --enforce-eager, kv_role=kv_producer
# decode:  --all2all-backend mori_low_latency --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"PIECEWISE"}', kv_role=kv_consumer
vllm serve /models/GLM-5.2-FP8 -tp 1 --data-parallel-size 8 --data-parallel-size-local 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend <backend> \
  --trust-remote-code --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 32768 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MoRIIOConnector","kv_role":"<role>", ...}'
```

DP4/TP2/EP8, single node:

```bash
vllm serve /models/GLM-5.2-FP8 -tp 2 -dp 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --all2all-backend mori_high_throughput \
  --trust-remote-code --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
  --max-model-len 32768 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --enforce-eager
# repeat with --all2all-backend allgather_reducescatter
```

GSM8K:

```bash
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 \
  --model_args model=/models/GLM-5.2-FP8,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,tokenized_requests=False \
  --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=512
```

## Test Result

| Layout | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |

commits.pr_title: [Perf] Share Triton JIT warmup compilation pool across registered kernels
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #58582. Eligible Triton kernels now share one `AsyncCompileMode` pool during startup warmup, instead of each kernel draining its own pool in turn.

## Claims

- Compilation now overlaps across kernels, not just within one kernel. Single-key kernels previously always compiled serially.
- 9–12% faster cold JIT warmup at default threads, 23–28% at 16 threads, when several Triton warmup kernels are registered (MRV1 sampler/spec-decode kernels, DSv4, GLM-5 Next).
- No change for ROCm, autotuned kernels, non-Triton owners, or configs with a single registered kernel.

## Validation

`pytest tests/model_executor/test_jit_warmup_triton_launcher.py`: 15 passed. The updated test (two single-key kernels must compile concurrently) fails on the base commit.

Cold-cache `JIT kernel warmup finished in …s` on H100, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`, mean of 3 runs per arm:

| Config | Threads | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gemma 4 31B + EAGLE3, TP=8 (12 kernels) | 4 | 20.72s | 18.86s (−9%) |
| | 16 | 15.25s | 11.69s (−23%) |
| Qwen3-0.6B-FP8 + ngram (9 kernels) | 4 | 17.99s | 15.89s (−12%) |
| | 16 | 11.55s | 8.37s (−28%) |

Gemma 4 on default MRV2 registers only the FA4 kernel, so there's nothing to overlap: 5.74s → 5.73s. No model evals: only compile scheduling changes, not the compiled kernels.

<details>
<summary>Repro</summary>

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 VLLM_TRITON_JIT_WARMUP_NUM_THREADS=16 \
TRITON_CACHE_DIR=$(mktemp -d) VLLM_CACHE_ROOT=$(mktemp -d) python -c "
from vllm import LLM
LLM('google/gemma-4-31b-it', tensor_parallel_size=8, max_model_len=8192,
    kernel_config={'enable_flashinfer_autotune': False},
    speculative_config={'method': 'eagle3', 'num_speculative_tokens': 3,
                        'model': 'RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-speculator.eagle3'})
" 2>&1 | grep 'JIT kernel warmup finished'
```

</details>

## Details

`JitWarmupRegistry.warmup()` runs all kernels with `supports_parallel_compile` inside one `compile_triton_warmup()` pool, then the rest serially. A ContextVar stops `compile_many` from nesting pools; called directly, it still creates its own pool. Dispatch stays on the calling thread, as in #58582.

Limitations:
- The tqdm bar advances on dispatch, so it jumps ahead and then waits for the pool to drain.
- Compile errors surface when the shared pool exits, not inside the failing kernel's `compile_many`.

Not a duplicate: no open PR shares a pool across kernels. #56154 (compile-key derivation) and #56761 (TileLang) are the closest.

---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Keep the parser's tool call IDs in batch derender
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Batch `/v1/chat/completions/derender` now keeps the parser's tool call IDs, the same as `/v1/chat/completions` and streaming derender. Part of #42729.

## Claims

- Batch derender uses `tc.id or make_tool_call_id()` in place of a bare `random_uuid()`. Default IDs get their `chatcmpl-tool-` prefix back and Kimi K2 style `functions.<name>:<idx>` IDs come through unchanged.
- The batch parity test compares tool call ID formats as well as names and arguments. It also gives derender the engine's `finish_reason` instead of the coupled one, so derender has to apply the `tool_calls` rewrite itself.

## Validation

New unit tests in `test_derender.py`. Both fail on `main` and pass with this change:

- `test_derender_chat_tool_call_id_matches_chat_completion`: real hermes parser, checks the ID starts with `chatcmpl-tool-`.
- `test_derender_chat_keeps_parser_tool_call_id`: a stub parser returns `functions.get_weather:1` and the test checks it's kept.

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py -v
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_parity.py -v
```

No model eval. The change only affects tool call IDs, not generated text.

## Details

Batch derender threw away the ID the parser had already built. Chat templates for Kimi-style models reference these IDs in multi-turn history, so a bare UUID breaks follow up turns. It also meant batch and streaming derender returned different IDs for the same tokens.

The parity test missed this because `_tool_sig` only looks at names and arguments. It also fed derender the coupled server's `finish_reason` which already had the `tool_calls` rewrite applied, so derender never had to work it out. #59324 shares `resolve_finish_reason()` between chat and derender, so the test can now pass the engine's value.

The current batch tool cases use a named `tool_choice` which never rewrites to `tool_calls`. So the `finish_reason` change mostly guards future auto tool cases.

This matters for #56851 too. The planned `parse_context` carries `history_tool_call_cnt` for Kimi IDs and that field does nothing while batch derender overwrites the IDs.

---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Honor the constructor chat template in offline scoring
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`LLM(chat_template=...).score(...)` ignores the constructor's template unless it is passed again to every `score()` call, so cross-encoder prompts are built without a template. For rerankers that need one, like Qwen3-Reranker, the scores are wrong. This makes offline scoring fall back to the constructor's template, as online scoring and offline `chat()` (#61061) already do.

## Claims

- `LLM.score()` uses the template passed to the `LLM` constructor when no `chat_template` is given to the call.
- A `chat_template` passed to `LLM.score()` still overrides it, and scoring without any template is unchanged.

## Validation

Unit tests (CPU, Python-only install):

```bash
python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_io_processor_unit.py -q
# main: 1 failed, 13 passed. This PR: 14 passed.
```

The new `test_offline_scoring_uses_default_template_unless_overridden` builds offline requests through `get_request_factory_offline` with a constructor template, a per-call template, both, or neither, renders them with `get_score_prompt` and checks the text and token IDs.

End to end on an L4, comparing the wheel for fa75d3456 (`main`) with the same wheel plus this change: `LLM("Qwen/Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B", runner="pooling", hf_overrides={"architectures": ["Qwen3ForSequenceClassification"], "classifier_from_token": ["no", "yes"], "is_original_qwen3_reranker": True}, chat_template=TEMPLATE, enforce_eager=True, dtype="bfloat16")`, where `TEMPLATE` is the reranker's query/document prompt, then `llm.score("What is the capital of France?", documents)`. The reference applies the same template with the tokenizer and takes the softmax over the "no"/"yes" logits of the Hugging Face model.

| Document | `main` | This PR | Hugging Face reference |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The capital of France is Paris. | 0.9829 | 0.9972 | 0.9973 |
| The capital of Germany is Berlin. | 0.9535 | 0.0984 | 0.1097 |
| Pasta is often served with tomato sauce. | 0.5200 | 0.0116 | 0.0115 |
| Prompt lengths (tokens) | 14 / 14 / 16 | 84 / 84 / 85 | 84 / 84 / 85 |

With this change the prompt token IDs match the templated reference exactly for all three documents, and the scores match the reference within `atol=0.01, rtol=0.02` (bf16).

`pre-commit run --files` on the four changed files: all hooks passed.

## Details

`PoolingOfflineMixin` passes the constructor's template to the scoring processors, and `CrossEncoderIOProcessor.get_request_factory_online` uses it (`self.chat_template`). `get_request_factory_offline` instead copied only `ctx.chat_template`, the template passed to `LLM.score()`, which defaults to `None`, so `get_score_prompt` took the path without a template. It now uses `self.chat_template` when `ctx.chat_template` is `None`. I updated the `score()` docstring, which said `None` means the model's default template, and added a sentence to the scoring docs.

Duplicate check: I searched open and closed PRs and issues for `LLM.score` with `chat_template`, "offline template ignored", `CrossEncoderIOProcessor chat_template` and the file paths. #61061 (merged) fixed the same fallback for `chat()`/`enqueue_chat()` but not `score()`. Open PRs that touch these files (#60877 saved CrossEncoder templates, #55359 CrossEncoder heads, #61772 token embeddings in `embed()`) don't change this fallback.

I used AI assistance (Claude) to find, fix and test this bug and to write this description.

---

commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Resolve logprobs on the parsed streaming derender path
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Streaming `/v1/chat/completions/derender` with a reasoning or tool parser returned no logprobs: #55029 resolved them only on the plain detokenization path, and the parser path built its stream choices without them. This PR resolves each chunk's logprobs on the parser path and mirrors the coupled endpoint's hidden-reasoning rule on both batch and streaming derender. Closes #59590.

## Claims

- On the parser path each generate chunk's `logprobs` are resolved once and attached to whatever delta the parser emits for that chunk (reasoning, content, tool-call delta, or an empty delta while the parser buffers markup), the same as `/v1/chat/completions`, which has one `logprobs.content` list regardless of field.
- The byte-fallback context now crosses chunks on the parser path through the existing `logprob_context_token_ids` tail, starting empty like the engine. `DerenderStreamState` is unchanged and replay never touches logprobs, as agreed on the issue.
- With a parser configured and `include_reasoning=false`, batch and streaming derender return no logprobs at all. Batch `_derender_chat` previously cleared `reasoning` but still returned them.
- No wire change. Chunks without `logprobs` still produce `logprobs: null`.

## Validation

GPU run on an A100-40G (branch overlaid onto `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-21d93d0d8c`, which is an ancestor of this branch):

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py \
       tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py
# 143 passed, 1 xfailed in 267s

pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_parity.py
# 12 passed, 7 skipped in 220s
```

All 7 parity skips are "Model did not emit a tool call" from `DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B`; 4 of them are pre-existing tool-call parity tests that skip on `main` for the same reason, even with `tool_choice` forced. The new reasoning and hidden-reasoning logprob parity cases pass on GPU.

Not compared against the coupled endpoint: the parser-swallowed chunk (`test_stream_parity_logprobs_tool_call` skips on the CI model) and the multi-byte split (`test_logprobs_multibyte_across_chunks`, unit only). Both are unit-tested on the real tokenizer and parser.

Locally: `pre-commit run --all-files` and `pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --all-files --hook-stage manual` clean.

New tests:

- `test_derender_stream.py` (unit, parser path): logprobs attached to each delta kind, kept when the parser swallows a chunk, dropped on every chunk with `include_reasoning=false`, a multi-byte character split across chunks, and the logprob context advancing on chunks without logprobs.
- `test_derender.py` (batch e2e): `test_e2e_parsed_logprobs_follow_include_reasoning`.
- `test_derender_parity.py` (streaming vs `/v1/chat/completions`): `test_stream_parity_logprobs_reasoning`, `test_stream_parity_logprobs_tool_call`, `test_stream_parity_logprobs_hidden_reasoning`. `utils.stream_chat_derender` gained `logprobs` and `raw_choices` parameters for these.

## Details

- **Why no replay cursor.** A generate chunk's `logprobs` cover exactly that chunk's tokens (the engine slices to the delta), so nothing is derived from replay and there is nothing to skip on re-emit. Only the 4-token byte-fallback context needs to persist, and the state already carries it (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/59590#issuecomment-5901337931).
- **Why suppress on every chunk.** Decoded logprob token strings would reveal the hidden reasoning text, so the coupled chat endpoint drops logprobs entirely for the request when a parser is configured and `include_reasoning` is false. Derender now does the same, batch and streaming.
- **Docs.** `docs/serving/online_serving/derenderer.md` updated to describe the parser path and the `include_reasoning` rule.

Duplicate-work check: searched open PRs for `59590 in:body`, `derender logprobs` and `parsed streaming logprobs`. The only hit referencing #59590 is #60082 (derender output mode on generate), which consumes this behaviour rather than implementing it. #59518 (merged 2026-10-15) changes which `top_logprobs` candidates derender keeps; since it landed first, this PR applies its `_chat_top_logprobs_limit` cut on the parser path too, as agreed on both PRs. #57790 is engine-side `LogprobsProcessor` handling for streaming input continuations, unrelated to derender.

---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Mooncake] Fix MultiConnector stats and proxy SSE responses
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Using direct Mooncake with Mooncake Store can fail in MultiConnector's metrics handler, and the Mooncake example proxy labels SSE responses as JSON, causing clients such as AIPerf to reject them. Fix both integration issues by respecting optional metrics exporters and returning the correct streaming Content-Type.

## Claims

- Skip children without Prometheus exporters while continuing to forward supported metrics and `engine_idx`.
- Return `text/event-stream` for streaming requests on `/v1/completions` and `/v1/chat/completions`; preserve JSON responses for non-streaming requests and forward response bytes unchanged.

```diff
 P transfer stats -> MultiConnector metrics
-  require an exporter for every child with stats
+  forward stats only to registered exporters

 D SSE frames -> Mooncake proxy -> client
-  Content-Type: application/json
+  Content-Type: text/event-stream
```

## Validation

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_proxy.py \
  -k 'TestMultiConnectorStats or test_mooncake_proxy' -q
```

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stats-only child, with empty or mixed exporter registry | Both regression cases fail on main `c75cb63cd2bb` | All 17 stats cases pass |
| Real ASGI routes, completion/chat × streaming/non-streaming | 2 streaming cases fail on main `258b97ff6bc1`; 2 non-streaming cases pass | All 4 cases pass |
| Combined PR branch, based on `258b97ff6bc1` | — | **21 passed, 15 deselected** |

The metrics regression also checks that the supported child's payload reaches its exporter with `engine_idx=2`. The proxy regression mocks only the remote P/D calls and checks the actual response headers and bytes. In Buildkite, the V1 KV Connectors step runs the metrics regression. The proxy regression is CPU-only, so it is marked `cpu_test` and runs in the CPU V1 Others step, which also lists the proxy as a source dependency so proxy-only changes still trigger it.

Changed-file pre-commit checks pass:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files \
  .buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml \
  examples/disaggregated/mooncake_connector/mooncake_connector_proxy.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/multi_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_proxy.py
```

Earlier ROCm end-to-end validation used integration commit `b41cf676db9cc124fffbcf305f7fa8c8d2f895b8`, containing the identical proxy file and metrics `observe()` implementation:

- [Before the proxy fix](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/38169410559): AIPerf attempted JSON parsing of SSE frames; all 13 sampled warmup responses were rejected.
- [C16 serving](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/38174661539): Kimi-K3 + DSpark3, 1P1D/16 MI355X, Mooncake RDMA + TCP Store completed a 3600-second performance window with 2006 successes and 4 errors. The workflow later failed while importing the separate GSM8K evaluator.
- [Natural GSM8K](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/actions/runs/38203116096): flexible extraction 1269/1319 (96.21%).

GPU evidence belongs to that integration revision; the current main-based PR branch has local regression coverage. Store lease timeouts and empty-response failures remain separate limitations. No additional GPU experiment was dispatched for this PR.

## Details

**Metrics:** `KVConnectorBase_V1.build_prom_metrics()` may return `None`. MultiConnector's metrics factory already excludes null exporters, while stats collection independently includes stats-only children. Direct Mooncake provides stats without an exporter, so its worker stats trigger the assertion in the API output handler. A conditional exporter lookup follows the existing optional-interface contract. Stats collection is unchanged; missing exporter IDs are skipped, so this assertion no longer detects inconsistent IDs in the metrics path.

**HTTP:** `_handle_completions` already forwards the request's streaming mode to D. Use the same flag to select the response media type. KV transfer and generation logic are unchanged.

The metrics portion follows up the **same fix proposed in #43836 for #43828**, adapted to the current flat stats payload with regression coverage. That PR remains open; this is not a distinct solution. The submitting operator explicitly requested including it here to cover both direct-Mooncake integration failures. Searches found no overlapping proxy SSE-header fix.

Both changes are reversible and scoped to metrics forwarding and the example proxy. AI assistance (Codex) was used; this remains a draft submitted at the human operator's request.

commits.pr_title: [Feature][PCP] Add DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash support
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Add text-only DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Prefill Context Parallelism (PCP) support on NVIDIA CUDA to Model Runner V2 with FlashMLA sparse attention.

This PR intentionally targets a colocated single-model instance only. P/D disaggregation and KV transfer are not supported in this initial scope. The implementation keeps compressed KV, indexer, SWA, Engram lookback, MoE routing inputs, and padding consistent across PCP ranks while closing ratio-2 pairs split across PCP chunks with gathered predecessor rows.

Related to #25749 and #49109. This PR targets the DeepSeek-V4.1 ratio-1/2 cache path and does not add the V4 C4/C128 or MegaMoE work from #43809.

## Supported Scope

- NVIDIA CUDA only: text-only DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on Model Runner V2 with `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41`.
- One colocated model instance with PP=DP=DCP=1.
- Prefill PCP with arbitrary PCP chunk boundaries, including ranks with no local decode requests.
- Tensor parallelism and PCP can be composed; the validation below covers TP8/PCP1, TP4/PCP2, and TP2/PCP4 on an 8-GPU node.
- Expert parallel execution with the `allgather_reducescatter` all-to-all backend.
- Eager execution with synchronous scheduling.

## Not Supported Yet

- P/D disaggregation or any KV connector.
- ROCm.
- Pipeline parallelism, data parallelism, decode context parallelism, or microbatching with PCP.
- Prefix caching or SWA bounded replay with PCP.
- Speculative decoding, CUDA graphs, or MegaMoE with PCP.
- Multimodal inputs, encoder-decoder models, or LoRA with PCP.
- Attention backends other than the DeepSeek-V4.1 FlashMLA sparse path.

These constraints are deliberate so the first upstream step establishes standalone PCP correctness without mixing in KV handoff or replay semantics. Follow-up work will expand one boundary at a time: first standalone cache/replay behavior, then additional single-instance parallel topologies and runtime features, and finally P/D disaggregation with a minimal direct connector before layering prefix caching, bounded replay, and speculative Decode support.

## Implementation

- Compress ratio-2 groups on each rank's local token rows. Gather only the last FP32 row of each local chunk to close cross-rank pairs and keep the open ring rows consistent.
- Keep PCP linkage in model-specific compressor metadata; `InputBatch` and `PCPManager` remain unchanged relative to `main`.
- Gather BF16 compressor latents in one cache-insert path shared with ratio 1, then use the aligned gathered positions and slots for main KV and Indexer K writes.
- Keep Engram lookback, MoE routing token IDs, padding, compressed KV, indexer keys, and SWA metadata aligned across PCP ranks.
- Keep PCP collectives ordered consistently across ranks, including empty local shards and requests with no local decode rows.

Engram embeddings remain TP-sharded, so increasing PCP can increase host memory requirements.

## Rank-local Compressor Revision

Following LucasWilkinson's review, this revision adopts [wangyicong52/vllm#1](https://github.com/wangyicong52/vllm/pull/1), authored by Lucas Wilkinson, at `b06bea7abc4eb5cf6965fe704d16257ac7c70697`. It removes the `InputBatch.pcp_metadata` / `PCPBatchMetadata` plumbing and the global FP32 `kv_score` gather.

Local validation of this revision: 101 passed, 6 CUDA-only skipped; applicable pre-commit hooks, mypy 3.10/3.12, syntax and diff checks passed. Additional CPU regressions cover PCP2/4 predecessor linkage, replicated short prefills, empty ranks, request isolation and newest open ring rows.

The GPU/model measurements below belong to the preceding global-order compressor implementation. They have not been rerun for this revision. The rank-local kernel, GSM8K and Prefill benchmark require renewed validation on the target H20 configuration before these historical results can support claims about this version.

## Validation Environment

- Hardware: one node with 8x NVIDIA H20 (96G, SM90) GPUs.
- SM100 was not validated in this PR.
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-92044241a02f05de51420d654daf669de20b4691`.

## vLLM Launch Arguments

Only the TP/PCP pair changed across the accuracy arms: `TP_SIZE=8, PCP_SIZE=1` for TP8/PCP1, `TP_SIZE=4, PCP_SIZE=2` for TP4/PCP2, and `TP_SIZE=2, PCP_SIZE=4` for TP2/PCP4. PP, DP, and DCP remained 1.

```bash
vllm serve /models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 18001 \
  --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --language-model-only \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla \
  --block-size 64 \
  --tensor-parallel-size "${TP_SIZE}" \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 1 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 1 \
  --prefill-context-parallel-size "${PCP_SIZE}" \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --all2all-backend allgather_reducescatter \
  --moe-backend marlin \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' \
  --max-model-len auto \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --no-swa-bounded-replay \
  --enforce-eager \
  --no-async-scheduling
```

## Validation

```bash
evalscope eval \
  --eval-type openai_api \
  --api-url http://<HOST>:18001/v1 \
  --api-key EMPTY \
  --model deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --model-id deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --datasets gsm8k \
  --dataset-hub modelscope \
  --dataset-args '{"gsm8k":{"few_shot_num":4}}' \
  --seed 42 \
  --eval-batch-size 64 \
  --generation-config '{"temperature":0.0,"top_p":1.0,"max_tokens":65536,"reasoning_effort":"high","seed":42,"timeout":10000}' \
  --timeout 10000
```

EvalScope's GSM8K report exposes extracted-answer `accuracy` and per-request `avg_output_tps`; it does not report separate exact-match or flexible-match metrics.

| Topology | Correct | Accuracy | Avg output tok/s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TP8/PCP1 baseline | 1281/1319 | 97.1190% | 7.36 |
| TP4/PCP2 | 1282/1319 | 97.1948% | 7.04 |
| TP2/PCP4 | 1284/1319 | 97.3465% | 7.10 |

The Prefill benchmark used `vllm bench serve` with exact-length random prompts, one output token, seed 42, prefix caching disabled, one warmup wave, and four measured waves. Results below include input tok/s and mean TTFT in milliseconds; values in parentheses are changes relative to the TP8/PCP1 baseline.

| Input tokens | Max concurrency | TP8/PCP1 input tok/s | TP4/PCP2 input tok/s | TP2/PCP4 input tok/s | TP8/PCP1 mean TTFT (ms) | TP4/PCP2 mean TTFT (ms) | TP2/PCP4 mean TTFT (ms) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8192 | 1 | 6763.52 | 7914.17 (+17.01%) | 8892.92 (+31.48%) | 1210.98 | 1034.90 (-14.54%) | 920.97 (-23.95%) |
| 8192 | 4 | 6963.35 | 8220.16 (+18.05%) | 9207.19 (+32.22%) | 4267.48 | 3614.73 (-15.30%) | 3227.61 (-24.37%) |
| 8192 | 8 | 6967.68 | 8242.67 (+18.30%) | 9215.61 (+32.26%) | 8377.18 | 7082.04 (-15.46%) | 6334.22 (-24.39%) |
| 16384 | 1 | 6705.38 | 7929.32 (+18.25%) | 8880.13 (+32.43%) | 2443.16 | 2065.99 (-15.44%) | 1844.79 (-24.49%) |
| 16384 | 4 | 6897.41 | 8184.03 (+18.65%) | 9184.73 (+33.16%) | 8616.79 | 7264.02 (-15.70%) | 6472.20 (-24.89%) |
| 16384 | 8 | 6905.88 | 8204.16 (+18.80%) | 9205.42 (+33.30%) | 16906.55 | 14230.82 (-15.83%) | 12682.85 (-24.98%) |
| 32768 | 1 | 6629.52 | 7896.71 (+19.11%) | 8818.36 (+33.02%) | 4942.36 | 4149.20 (-16.05%) | 3715.34 (-24.83%) |
| 32768 | 4 | 6797.97 | 8121.66 (+19.47%) | 9136.55 (+34.40%) | 17484.04 | 14635.41 (-16.29%) | 13010.39 (-25.59%) |
| 32768 | 8 | 6816.65 | 8135.74 (+19.35%) | 9163.40 (+34.43%) | 34265.77 | 28708.44 (-16.22%) | 25490.96 (-25.61%) |

## Humming Validation

Upstream PR #56997 (`[Quantization] Prefer Humming before Marlin backends on SM90`) changed `main` so SM90 MXFP4 automatic selection prefers Humming over Marlin for both linear and MoE kernels. Under PCP, TP4/PCP2 initially exposed a Humming permute-scratch capacity mismatch: PCP gathered 8,192 token rows while the old formula allocated 4,096 rows.

We revalidated this with upstream PR #60447, which replaces the configuration-derived capacity formula with a general input-sized scratch that grows during warmup and is fixed after the workspace manager locks. The validation used #60447 head `44ea227814` plus this PR's two commits, with no #60423 overlay. Both TP4/PCP2 and TP2/PCP4 selected `HUMMING` MXFP4 MoE and `HummingMxfp8LinearKernel`, matched all 206 overlaid runtime files, and completed startup with zero Pod restarts and no scratch or workspace-lock assertion.

The Humming run used `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-21d93d0d8c0e9627900020382bfce4730e61cab7` on one 8x H20 (SM90) node. The exact random Prefill matrix used one output token, seed 42, prefix caching disabled, one warmup wave, and four measured waves. EvalScope GSM8K used all 1,319 records, four-shot prompts, batch size 64, seed 42, temperature 0, top-p 1, and `max_tokens=65536`.

### Humming GSM8K

| Topology | Correct | Accuracy | Avg output tok/s | API errors | Length finishes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| TP4/PCP2 | 1282/1319 | 97.1948% | 6.31 | 0 | 1 |
| TP2/PCP4 | 1286/1319 | 97.4981% | 6.19 | 0 | 0 |

### Humming Prefill Performance

|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TP4/PCP2 | 5554.72 | 5548.94 | +0.10% |
| TP2/PCP4 | 5925.67 | 5917.19 | +0.14% |

The #60447 run has no measurable Prefill regression relative to the preceding Humming validation. Humming remains materially below the corresponding Marlin measurements, so the documented launch command remains pinned to Marlin.

One TP4/PCP2 GSM8K sample is a quality and latency caveat: sample 119 reached `max_tokens=65536` after 9,701 seconds, while the matching TP2/PCP4 sample stopped naturally at 10,096 tokens. The TP4 result should therefore not be read as token-identical or as a clean quality-equivalence claim. This did not reproduce as a runtime failure: both topologies completed with zero API errors, zero Pod restarts, and zero critical server errors.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Honor code_revision in config-based tokenizer loading
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Honor `ModelConfig.code_revision` in both config-based tokenizer helpers when the model and tokenizer share a repository. Complements #61272, which fixed snapshot resolution for direct tokenizer loading.

## Claims

- Config-based loading no longer silently ignores an independently pinned tokenizer code revision.
- A separately configured tokenizer does not inherit an unrelated model commit.
- Explicit caller overrides, including `code_revision=None`, remain authoritative.

## Validation

### Config-code pin follow-up (`4a34bfa32d`)

`get_tokenizer` now forwards the resolved `code_revision` to `get_config`, so the remote AutoConfig module follows the same pin as tokenizer code. This is an appended commit; earlier reviewed commits are unchanged.

- New regression uses real HF dynamic config loading from `hf-internal-testing/test_dynamic_model`, with only tokenizer instantiation replaced. Default and matching revisions pass before the fix; a distinct pin fails because the loaded config class comes from the data revision. Negative control: **1 failed, 2 passed**. With the fix, the full code-revision selection is **26 passed, 5 deselected**.
- Registry, generate-stream and LoRA resolver suites: **109 passed** in the existing native Linux CPU validation container.
- All applicable pinned pre-commit hooks pass, including mypy and Buildkite test tethering.
- A separate real-backend smoke probe (no tokenizer-loader replacement) used local tokenizer assets with a remote AutoConfig reference. Baseline loaded config code from `c8ae8a2e5845fc3ad4e5237e4346e5a9ba1e87d2`; the fix loaded the requested `2efddce40dddaccd37bae208c3c7ca66dbedf68a`. Both encoded `hello world` to `[1, 2]`. This is tokenizer validation, not model inference or a new HTTP serving test.

### Review follow-up (`554c1c1842`)

Both review findings are addressed: resolved Mistral mode drops the HF-only `code_revision` key; both config helpers tolerate a missing attribute and no longer inject unset revisions. HF-backed aliases and explicit caller overrides remain supported.

Native pytest was rerun in the existing Linux CPU container (Python 3.12.13, Torch 2.13.0+cpu, Transformers 5.19.0, pytest 9.1.1), with this worktree's Python package and tests copied into an isolated `/validation/pr61611` directory. No AST extraction was used for these results.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `python -m pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_registry.py -q --tb=short` | 57 passed; original PR registry with the new tests: 20 failed, 37 passed |
| `python -m pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_basic.py -k code_revision -q --tb=short` | 23 passed, 5 deselected (includes 8 real Mistral backend cases) |
| `python -m pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_basic.py -k config_mistral_code_revision -q --tb=no` against the original PR registry | All 8 failed; real backend rejects `code_revision` |
| `python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_generate_stream.py tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_lora_resolvers.py -q --tb=short` | 52 passed, without changing their minimal config stubs |
| `pre-commit run --files vllm/tokenizers/registry.py tests/tokenizers_/test_registry.py tests/tokenizers_/test_basic.py` | All applicable hooks passed, including mypy and Buildkite test tethering |

The Mistral tests load `mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3` through both helpers in explicit and auto modes, with `code_revision=None` and `"never"`. Original registry behavior was tested in the same environment with automatic restoration of the fixed file. Warnings were Torch JIT deprecations and the existing `TestTokenizer` collection warning. These are real tokenizer/backend tests, not model-weight loading, inference/GPU evaluation, or a new HTTP serving test.

### Initial validation

Linux x86_64, Python 3.12.13, Torch 2.13.0+cpu, Transformers 5.19.0. Validation reused a native environment based on e0317b28 with the relevant current modules and tests copied in; it was not a complete native rebuild of b9b401b2ef.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Config/code-revision regressions against baseline | 4 failed, 11 passed, 5 deselected: both helpers silently accepted unknown or missing-code revisions |
| Same tests with this fix | 15 passed, 5 deselected |
| `tests/tokenizers_/test_registry.py` | 7 passed |
| Applicable pre-commit hooks on all three changed files | Passed, including mypy and Buildkite test tethering |
| `git diff --check` | Passed |

A real `ModelConfig` → `VllmConfig` → renderer integration also verified separate-repository loading and explicit `None` overrides.

A real no-weights `vllm launch render` HTTP reproducer confirmed:
- Baseline: unknown and missing-code revisions incorrectly allow startup and HTTP 200 from `/tokenize`.
- Fixed: both are rejected during tokenizer initialization with the corresponding Transformers `OSError`.
- Fixed matching revision: HTTP 200 with token IDs `[1, 0, 0, 2]`.

### How to Test

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_basic.py -k code_revision -v --tb=short
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_registry.py -v --tb=short
pre-commit run --files vllm/tokenizers/registry.py tests/tokenizers_/test_basic.py tests/tokenizers_/test_registry.py
```

For manual reproduction, use `hf-internal-testing/test_dynamic_tokenizer` as both model and tokenizer, pinned to `08a35780b7a78794436d8654aafa26ee0165c149`, with `--tokenizer-mode hf --trust-remote-code --max-model-len 32`. The tokenizer-only fixture needs `--hf-config-path` pointing to a real cached OPT config (tested with `facebook/opt-125m` at `27dcfa74d334bc871f3234de431e71c6eeba5dd6`). Keep Hub access enabled. Set `--code-revision never` or `73293ac504e43f4a895688b57c65cebe24f01a38`: baseline starts, but this fix rejects the requested code. A matching code revision starts successfully and `/tokenize` returns the control token IDs above.

## Details

Both `tokenizer_args_from_config` and `cached_tokenizer_from_config` omitted the model's code revision. They now use `setdefault` and the same model/tokenizer repository equality guard already used by the processor chat-template path. This avoids applying a model commit to an independently configured tokenizer repository. The skip-tokenizer-init early return is unchanged.

- `vllm/tokenizers/registry.py`: guarded code-revision propagation in both wrappers.
- `tests/tokenizers_/test_basic.py`: real remote-code loading regressions for both helpers, separate repositories and explicit overrides; real Mistral config-loading regressions; accept equivalent offline errors in the existing negative test.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Structured Output] Mask grammar-invalid implicit reasoning ends
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

With an engine-based reasoning parser, a structured-output request fails with "grammar rejected tokens" and HTTP 500 when the model samples an implicit reasoning end, such as GLM's `<tool_call>`, that the request's grammar cannot start with. Reasoning rows of the bitmask are unconstrained, so the token can be sampled, and since #59627 it is fed to the grammar. This masks those tokens while the request reasons. Implicit ends the grammar accepts stay allowed.

Related: #60722 (RFC; this is the "remaining issue" it describes, using its first option restricted to grammar-rejected tokens), #59627 (feeds the implicit end to the grammar), #59608 (`required`/named tool calls, which must keep `<tool_call>` allowed), #61456 (open; also edits `_fill_bitmasks`).

## Claims

- A request whose grammar rejects an implicit reasoning end as its first token (a JSON schema, `tool_choice="none"` with `response_format`) can no longer sample that token while reasoning, so it no longer ends in "grammar rejected tokens".
- Requests whose grammar accepts the implicit end are unchanged: `tool_choice` `required`, named, and `auto` with tools (with or without `response_format`).
- The explicit end (`</think>`) and every other token stay allowed while reasoning. Draft and bonus rows under speculative decoding are masked the same way.

## Validation

**Unit, CPU.** `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`, xgrammar and guidance:

```text
python -m pytest tests/v1/structured_output/test_structured_output_manager.py \
  tests/parser/engine/test_parser_engine.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_structured_output.py
# main source + these tests: 181 passed, 8 failed, 1 xfailed
# this branch:               189 passed, 1 xfailed
```

The 8 that fail on main: `test_real_flow[implicit_end_rejected-*]` (pattern `RRUUU`; main gives `UUUUU`), `test_reasoning_rows_mask_grammar_invalid_implicit_end[json-*]`, `test_parallel_fill_masks_grammar_invalid_implicit_end[*]`, and the two `TestReasoningEndTokenIds` cases for the new property. `test_reasoning_rows_mask_grammar_invalid_implicit_end[regex_starts_with_marker-*]` passes on both: a grammar that starts with the marker keeps it allowed and consumes it.

Wider run on this branch: `tests/v1/structured_output`, `tests/parser` (without `tests/parser/cohere`, which needs `cohere_melody`), `tests/reasoning/test_glm4_moe_reasoning_parser.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_grammar_invalid_drafts.py`, `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_structured_output.py`: 6636 passed, 1 xfailed. `tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py`: 19 passed on both. `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`: the same 48 multimodal tests fail on main and on this branch, because this kernel-less install cannot inspect the Llava architecture.

**Real components, no model.** GLM-5.3 tokenizer, `--reasoning-parser glm45` (`Glm47MoeParserReasoningAdapter`), xgrammar, prompt ending in `<think>`. Bitmask rows while reasoning, then `accept_tokens([<tool_call>])` as the scheduler would call it:

| constraint | main: `<tool_call>` allowed / masked bits | this branch | `accept_tokens` |
|---|---|---|---|
| JSON schema, no spec | yes / 0 | no / 1 (`<tool_call>` only; `</think>` allowed) | False |
| JSON schema, 3 draft rows + bonus | yes / 0 in all 4 rows | no / 1 in all 4 rows | False |
| `required` structural tag | yes / 0 | yes / 0 | True |
| named structural tag | yes / 0 | yes / 0 | True |

**End to end, CPU server.** arm64 CPU image of main `206e45d47`, whose four changed files are identical to `a2fb48273`, with the structured-output backends from `a2fb48273` mounted in both arms and this branch's four files in the second. A 2-layer Llama with the GLM-5.3 tokenizer and vocabulary, `--reasoning-parser glm45 --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice`, xgrammar, greedy, 3 runs per case. `logit_bias` makes `<tool_call>` (154843) the top token.

| request | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `json_schema`, bias `<tool_call>` | 500 x3, "grammar rejected tokens [154843]" | 200 x3, no `<tool_call>` in reasoning |
| `json_schema` + tools + `tool_choice="none"`, same bias | 500 x3 | 200 x3 |
| `json_schema`, bias `<tool_call>` 100, `</think>` 50, answer tokens 30 | 500 x3 | 200 x3, `{"answer": "yes"}`, finish `stop` |
| `json_schema` + tools + `tool_choice="auto"`, same bias | 200 x3, tool call | 200 x3, same tool call |
| `tool_choice="required"` / named / `auto` without `response_format` | 200 x3 each, tool call | 200 x3 each, same tool call |
| `json_schema`, no bias | 200 x3 | 200 x3 |

Every request that returns 200 on main returns the same response on this branch. The engine log on main has one `Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens [154843]` per 500 (12 of 12); the branch logs have none.

<details>
<summary>Raw request and responses (third row)</summary>

```json
{"model": "glm-tiny", "max_tokens": 96, "temperature": 0,
 "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Is the sky blue? Reply as JSON."}],
 "response_format": {"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {"name": "a", "schema": {
   "type": "object", "properties": {"answer": {"type": "string", "enum": ["yes", "no"]}},
   "required": ["answer"], "additionalProperties": false}}},
 "logit_bias": {"154843": 100, "154842": 50, "4913": 30, "9214": 30, "788": 30, "330": 30,
                "9689": 30, "9204": 30, "154820": 30}}
```

main, 3 of 3:

```text
HTTP 500 {"error":{"message":"Internal server error","type":"InternalServerError","param":null,"code":500}}
(EngineCore pid=131) ERROR 10-14 06:31:44 [scheduler.py:2189] Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens [154843] for request chatcmpl-8bf78d42551e682d-8a4ad66a. Terminating request.
```

this branch, 3 of 3 (fields from the response):

```text
HTTP 200  finish_reason=stop  reasoning="" (no <tool_call>)  content={"answer": "yes"}  tool_calls=[]
```
</details>

**Speculative decoding, end to end.** `logit_bias` is rejected with speculative decoding, so these runs use fixed weights instead: layer outputs are zero and the LM head prefers `<tool_call>`, then ` the`, at every position. ngram, 3 speculative tokens, `json_schema`, 96 tokens:

| | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `json_schema` | 500 x3 | 200 x3, 96 reasoning tokens, all ` the` |
| `json_schema` + tools + `tool_choice="none"` | 500 x3 | 200 x3 |
| drafts accepted (`json_schema` only) | | 207 of 225 |
| `required`, `auto` + tools | tool calls | same tool calls |

Each accepted draft position used a masked row; an unmasked draft row would have sampled `<tool_call>` and failed the request.

<details>
<summary>CPU harness note</summary>

On main the CPU stand-in `_compute_slot_mapping_kernel_impl` (`vllm/utils/cpu_triton_utils.py`) takes its arguments in an order that no longer matches `ComputeSlotMappingKernel.kernel`, so the dispatcher passes `slot_mapping` as `block_size` and the first forward fails. These runs mount a copy of that one function, with the kernel's parameter names, in both arms. Separate from this change.
</details>

**GPU, end to end.** @simon-veitner-redhat ran main `a2fb482732` against this branch `6d144d6478` on H200 ([results](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61574#issuecomment-6163972357)): GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4, TP2, `glm47` tool and reasoning parsers, xgrammar, 8 seeds per row. "Tagged" means a tool result in the conversation quotes GLM's own tags (`<tool_call>`, `<arg_key>`, `<arg_value>`), followed by a `json_schema` request.

| request, no spec decode | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| tagged, `json_schema`, no tools | 7/8 500s, 0/8 valid JSON | 0 500s, 4/8 valid JSON |
| tagged, `json_schema`, `tool_choice: "none"` | 5/8 500s, 3/8 valid JSON | 0 500s, 7/8 valid JSON |
| `logit_bias` forcing `<tool_call>`, blocking `</think>` | 8/8 500s | 0 500s, empty content |
| untagged, `json_schema` | 8/8 valid JSON | 8/8 valid JSON |
| tagged, `tool_choice: "required"` | 0 duplicated `<tool_call>` | 0 duplicated `<tool_call>` |

| request, MTP 3 tokens, Model Runner V2, async scheduling | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| tagged, `json_schema`, no tools | 6/8 500s, 2/8 valid JSON | 0 500s, 6/8 valid JSON |
| tagged, `json_schema`, `tool_choice: "none"` | 2/8 500s, 6/8 valid JSON | 0 500s, 8/8 valid JSON |
| untagged, `json_schema` | 8/8 valid JSON | 8/8 valid JSON |
| tagged, `tool_choice: "required"` | 0 duplicated `<tool_call>` | 0 duplicated `<tool_call>` |

Main logs one `Failed to advance FSM` per 500; this branch logs none. The remaining invalid JSON on this branch is a separate frontend issue: the token stream is valid JSON, but the model quotes `<tool_call>` inside a JSON string and `content` is cut there. The CPU runs above use the V1 model runner, so both runners are covered.

**Motivation.** A GLM-5.3 deployment (MTP with 3 tokens, Model Runner V2, xgrammar, `glm45`) logged 649 "grammar rejected tokens" terminations in 8 hours; 625 of them ended on `<tool_call>` (154843). A non-streaming request terminated this way returns HTTP 500.

## Details

Path of the failure, `enable_in_reasoning=False`:

1. A request with a JSON schema is reasoning. `_get_constraint_bounds` puts `constraint_start` past every scheduled row, so `grammar_bitmask` fills each row with the full mask.
2. The model samples `<tool_call>`, which `Glm47MoeParser` treats as an implicit reasoning end: it ends reasoning and starts a tool call.
3. `accept_tokens` finds that end and, since #59627, sets `grammar_start` to its offset, so `<tool_call>` is fed to the grammar. A JSON grammar rejects it and `accept_tokens` returns False.
4. The scheduler logs "Unexpected: grammar rejected tokens" and finishes the request with `FINISHED_ERROR`.

The change, in `StructuredOutputManager`:

- `ParserEngine.implicit_reasoning_end_token_ids`: reasoning-end tokens other than the explicit end, the same split `find_reasoning_end` uses to report an implicit end. Exposed through `ParserEngineReasoningAdapter`. This only adds a read-only property, so no parser changes behavior.
- `_masked_reasoning_ends`: the implicit ends the grammar rejects as its first token (`validate_tokens([t])`, non-mutating in every backend). The grammar does not advance before reasoning ends, so the set is computed once per request and cached on `StructuredOutputRequest`.
- `_fill_bitmasks`: a row the grammar does not constrain allows every token except those ids. Only rows before `constraint_start` (including the bonus row while reasoning) get them, in both the serial and the parallel fill. Constrained rows and rows after padding are unchanged.

Tradeoffs and limits:

- This changes the reasoning distribution only by removing tokens whose sampling makes the output invalid under the request's own constraint. The model keeps reasoning or ends with the explicit end. The alternative outcome is an error, so there is no flag.
- Same scope as #59627: engine-based parsers and single-token implicit ends. Multi-token or text-only ends (`deepseek_v4`, `inkling`) are not covered.
- Cost: one `validate_tokens` call per implicit end per request, and a bit clear per masked id on reasoning rows. No device work and no host sync.
- #61456 replaces the guidance path of `_fill_bitmasks` with a batch fill. Whichever lands second has to keep the reasoning-row mask.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Honor OPT token embedding width for prompt embeddings
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #61709. Use OPT's token embedding width for prompt embedding validation and runner buffers so `facebook/opt-350m` works with `--enable-prompt-embeds`.

## Claims

- Accept OPT-350m's 512-wide prompt embeddings and reject its incompatible 1024-wide hidden states.
- Allocate 512-wide input buffers for both model runners, matching `embed_input_ids()` and the decoder's `project_in` input.
- Preserve CLIP/SigLIP text embedding validation when their projection width differs from their hidden size.

## Validation

Review follow-up: CI scripts are unchanged. OPT-350m retains GPU generation coverage and is omitted from the offline CPU model matrix, whose cache lacks its weights; existing OPT-125m CPU coverage remains. The completion-renderer mock exposes the text config, and tokenizer setup uses the existing bounded retry helper. Follow-up checks: 57 renderer/width tests passed; both OPT-350m GPU cases remain selected, and neither is selected by `-m cpu_model`. Earlier CI-fix validation also passed 148 renderer/validation tests and 12 GPT-J streaming tests (4 skipped).



Tested in WSL on an RTX 3050 (8 GiB), Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu132, and Transformers 5.19.0. **202 pytest cases passed**, plus live HTTP and baseline reproduction checks.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Original OPT-350m config and validation | 512-wide inputs rejected; incompatible 1024-wide inputs accepted; buffer width 1024 |
| Fixed OPT-350m config and validation | 512-wide inputs accepted; 1024-wide inputs rejected; buffer width 512 |
| Prompt payload, sparse tensor, and completion validation | 113 passed |
| Chat prompt embedding parsing and GPU overlay kernels | 85 passed |
| OPT-350m generation evaluation, V2 runner | 2 passed, prompt embeddings enabled/disabled |
| OPT-350m generation evaluation, legacy runner | 2 passed, prompt embeddings enabled/disabled |
| Live HTTP completions | Single/batched embeddings match token-ID generation; streaming matches; wrong width returns 400; server remains healthy |
| Pre-commit hooks and whitespace | Passed, including Ruff, mypy, SPDX, and test CI tethering |

Generation evaluations use the existing Hugging Face/vLLM greedy generation and top-5 log-probability comparison over 32 generated tokens. With prompt embeddings enabled, they also compare token-ID and embedding generation. Both runners were tested with compilation/CUDA graphs; HTTP validation additionally exercised eager mode and chunked prefill.

<details>
<summary>Test commands and local configuration</summary>

```bash
PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/renderers/test_prompt_embeds_payload_validation.py \
  tests/renderers/test_sparse_tensor_validation.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_prompt_validation.py \
  -k 'not empty_prompt and not out_of_vocab' --tb=short -q

PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/renderers/chat_utils/test_prompt_embeds.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_prompt_embeds_state.py --tb=short -q

PYTHONPATH=. VLLM_PLUGINS= .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/language/generation/test_common.py -k opt-350m --tb=short -xv

PYTHONPATH=. VLLM_PLUGINS= VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 \
  VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/language/generation/test_common.py -k opt-350m --tb=short -xv

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only HEAD^ HEAD)
git diff --check HEAD^ HEAD
```

For the local 8 GiB GPU, a pytest plugin set `VllmRunner` defaults to `gpu_memory_utilization=0.65`, `attention_config={"backend": "TRITON_ATTN"}`, and `max_num_batched_tokens=1024`; the evaluation commands above require equivalent overrides on similarly constrained GPUs. Legacy runner testing used the supported PyTorch sampler because FlashInfer sampling warmup requires `nvcc`, which is absent from this WSL environment. Compiled libraries and the wheel-supplied FlashMLA interface were reused from the existing installation. No CUDA/C++ sources changed.

The HTTP server used `--enable-prompt-embeds --dtype float16 --enforce-eager --gpu-memory-utilization 0.65 --max-model-len 128 --max-num-seqs 4 --max-num-batched-tokens 16 --enable-chunked-prefill --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN`.

</details>

## Details

OPT-350m embeds tokens at `word_embed_proj_dim=512`, then projects them to `hidden_size=1024` inside the decoder. Buffer allocation and request validation previously used 1024, causing startup/input-copy failures and accepting embeddings that `project_in` cannot consume.

Add `word_embed_proj_dim` to the input-buffer size lookup and use it for request validation when present. Validation otherwise retains `get_hidden_size()`: using the buffer accessor wholesale would change CLIP/SigLIP validation to their projection width. Both runners share the corrected buffer accessor; no runner-specific branches or inference synchronization are added.

Regression coverage extends existing suites with actual OPT-350m/OPT-125m/CLIP/SigLIP configurations and adds OPT-350m to the model registry and generation comparison matrix. Duplicate searches for `61709 in:body` and `word_embed_proj_dim` found no open PR addressing this fix.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] Any-shape low-latency MoE router GEMM on MI355
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On MI355 (gfx950), the MoE router GEMM now has a low-latency kernel for **any** router shape (fp32 or bf16 weights, fp32 output, M ≤ 32), matching the CuTeDSL `ll_fp32w` / `ll_bf16` router kernels from #44343 and #50174. Previously only five hard-coded `(hidden_size, num_experts)` shapes had a fast path; every other model paid 9–13 µs per MoE layer per decode step in `F.linear` / hipBLASLt.

## Claims

- **Decode 1–14% faster** on all 8 tested MoE models whose router path changes, largest at low concurrency.
- **No accuracy change**: GSM8K matches `main` on every model (paired McNemar p = 1.0 and 0.34 where runs varied most).
- **No regressions**: prefill, an unchanged-path control (Qwen3-30B-A3B) and the 5 previously tuned shapes stay flat; shapes where the kernel would lose keep today's path.
- **New MI355 CI job** mirroring `(B200) Gate Linear CuTeDSL Kernels`.

Changes:

- Generalize `rocm_fp32_router_gemm` to any shape: masked K tail, MI355-swept launch rule, bf16 weights, size guards
- `GateLinear`: enable the fp32 router tier on gfx950 for any shape and route bf16-weight fp32-logit gates (tier 6) through the same dispatch op
- Extend `test_rocm_fp32_router_gemm.py` and fix the now-outdated rejection test in `test_gate_linear_rocm_dispatch.py`
- Add `:amd: (MI355) Gate Linear Router Kernels` (B200 mirror + optional `test-amd.yaml` entry) and move the 3 ROCm router test files there from MI355 Misc

## Validation

`main` vs this PR, end to end on MI355 (decode TPOT Δ, + is faster; median of 5 reps):

| Model | Router | Decode Δ C1 / C8 / C32 | GSM8K main → PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| ERNIE-4.5-21B-A3B | fp32 2560×64 | **+14.1 / +3.4 / +2.1%** | 86.58 → 86.28 |
| Trinity-Nano | fp32 1024×128 | **+9.6 / +4.9 / +4.0%** | 79.08 → 79.00 |
| Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-FP8 | fp32 2688×128 | **+9.4 / +5.4 / +2.2%** | 90.96 / 90.69 (A/A) → 90.83 |
| Ling-mini-2.0 | fp32 2048×256 | **+7.7 / +4.6 / +2.5%** | 88.02 → 88.10 |
| GLM-4.5-Air-FP8 (TP2) | fp32 4096×128 | **+5.0 / +5.0 / +2.9%** | 72.33 → 72.02 |
| Step-3.5-Flash-FP8 (TP2) | fp32 4096×288 | **+4.7 / +3.1 / +2.7%** | 89.61 → 89.31 |
| Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it | bf16 2816×128 | **+8.9 / +5.5 / +3.5%** | 94.31 → 94.39 |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash (TP2) | bf16 4096×256 | **+2.0 / +1.2 / +1.0%** | 95.80 → 95.86 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B (control) | unchanged | −0.2 / 0.0 / +0.2% | 91.66 → 91.58 |

8K prefill TTFT is flat on every model (within ±0.7%).

<details>
<summary>Methodology and accuracy details</summary>

- `vllm bench serve`, random dataset, prefix caching off, 1–8 input / 256–512 output tokens. `main` and the PR were served at the same time on separate GPUs, alternating every run, with GPU load logged each rep.
- GSM8K: lm_eval 5-shot chat, median of 3+ runs.
- Nemotron and DeepSeek-V4 were re-run with `--log_samples` for a paired per-question test. Nemotron PR vs `main`: 9 / 9 discordant, McNemar p = 1.0; `main` vs `main` A/A: 9 / 6, p = 0.61. DeepSeek-V4: 3 / 7 in the PR's favor, p = 0.34. An earlier DeepSeek-V4 round read 96.06 → 95.53; the repeat did not reproduce it.
- ERNIE's −0.7% prefill is within the 0.3–0.5% spread between GPUs, which a GPU-swap A/B confirmed. Trinity's prefill TTFT ranges overlap.
- **Why decode improves:** one router GEMM per MoE layer per step drops from 9–13 µs (`F.linear`) or 5–11 µs (hipBLASLt) to 1.9–4.9 µs at ≤ 8 tokens, saving 0.2–0.6 ms per step. Prefill and large batches never reach the kernel.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Kernel benchmark</summary>

MI355, one idle GPU, median of 30 graph replays, 2 runs with ≤5% drift. M = 1–32.

| | Shapes | vs today's path |
|---|---|---|
| fp32, the 5 old shapes | 5 | 0.97–1.30× vs old tuned configs (median 1.07×) |
| fp32, new shapes (DeepSeek-V3, Kimi-K2, Qwen3, Qwen3.8, gpt-oss, Llama4) | 7 | **1.2–6.8×** vs `F.linear` (median 4.1×) |
| fp32, held out from the sweep (GLM-4.5, Ernie, 1000×100, 1024 experts, …) | 10 | **1.1–7.0×**; two 1024-expert M=32 cases keep `F.linear` |
| bf16 | 9 | **1.7–5.4×** vs hipBLASLt at M ≤ 8, 1.04–2.9× at 16–32; never slower |

Max relative error vs float64: 1.3e-7 (fp32 weights), 8.9e-8 (bf16 weights).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Tests</summary>

- New CI command `pytest -v -s tests/kernels/test_rocm_fp32_router_gemm.py tests/kernels/test_gate_linear_rocm_dispatch.py tests/kernels/test_bf16x3_router_gemm_rocm.py`: 847 passed, 10/10 loops, ~5 min each.
- Each new test fails against a mutated kernel or dispatcher: no K-tail mask, the old shape list, a bypassed dispatcher, no bf16 cutoff, or no gfx950 tier-6 routing.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Design details, scope and related PRs</summary>

- **Launch rule:** one program computes `BLOCK_M` tokens for one expert. Narrow routers (< 64 experts) keep `BLOCK_M = 1`; wide routers grow it with the token count. Fitted on 12 shapes, checked on 10 held-out shapes: within 1.11× of the per-shape best and faster than the fallback everywhere.
- **Size guards:** at M·N·K ≥ 2^27 (fp32) or tokens × experts > 8192 (bf16) the fallback is faster, so the kernel declines and today's path runs.
- **Compile safety:** runtime branching stays inside the existing `fp32_router_gemm_dispatch` custom op.
- **Scope:** gfx950 only; gfx942, CUDA, biased/quantized gates and batch-invariant mode are unchanged.
- **Not covered end to end:** MiniMax-M2.5-MXFP4 decodes at ~196 ms/token on both `main` and the PR, so the difference is unmeasurable. Kimi-Linear-48B and LongCat-Flash-Lite-FP8 crash on unmodified `main`, unrelated to this change. Their router shapes are covered by the kernel tests.
- **Related PRs:** #59023 does the bf16 extension for Kimi-K3's 7168×896 gate only (this PR gives the same M ≤ 9 limit there, for any shape). #57626 forces fp32 weights for the 5 listed shapes instead; this PR runs bf16 weights directly with no fp32 copy. #61687 targets a separate AITER tier and is orthogonal.

</details>

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

commits.pr_body:
## Overview (this PR description was manually written by me) This is an NVIDIA-developed specialized implementation of Kimi K3 for GB300 that achieves 1.5-2x decode speedups. It supports: - TP8 and TP16 on GB300 - NoSpec (up to B64) and DSpark verification with 3-7 draft tokens (up to 64 tokens -- B8 for DL7, B16 for DL3) - Decode context parallelism with DCP=TP (DCP-off also supported) It is enabled opt-in via `--additional-config '{"decode_backend": "latency_specialized"}'`. All changes are localized to `vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/`. ## Claims With FP8 KV Cache, FP32 SSM Cache, and model-provider weights: - TP16, ISL 1, no speculation: decode step **1.79-1.92x faster than stock at B1-B8** (3.90 vs 7.38 ms at B1). - TP16, DSpark DL7, synthetic acceptance 6: **1.53-1.71x decode tok/s at B1-B8**. - DL7, ISL 32k, DCP on: **1.36-1.50x (TP8)** and **1.53-1.75x (TP16)** decode tok/s. - AIME25, GPQA-Diamond and MRCR v2 8-needle match stock within about one standard error, with and without speculation. ## Validation ### Correctness Testing Evals for this branch ran with DCP = TP (TP8+DCP8 and TP16+DCP16); stock ran on TP8 without DCP, C2 and C8 pooled. Spec on = DSpark DL7 with probabilistic drafting and standard rejection sampling (no forced acceptance). Score ± standard error, n samples per cell; pooling ours' C2 and C8 cells gives AIME25 avg@4, GPQA-Diamond avg@2, GSM8k avg@2. MRCR v2: 8-needle, (128k, 256k] contexts, thinking on, 32k output cap. | Task | Spec | Stock TP8 | Ours TP8+DCP8 C2 | Ours TP8+DCP8 C8 | Ours TP16+DCP16 C2 | Ours TP16+DCP16 C8 | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | AIME25 | off | 0.867 ± 0.033 (n=120) | 0.867 ± 0.048 | 0.917 ± 0.035 | 0.900 ± 0.037 | 0.900 ± 0.037 | | AIME25 | DL7 | 0.892 ± 0.032 (n=120) | 0.917 ± 0.042 | 0.900 ± 0.037 | 0.883 ± 0.052 | 0.950 ± 0.037 | | GPQA-D | off | 0.924 ± 0.011 (n=594) | 0.919 ± 0.019 | 0.914 ± 0.020 | 0.919 ± 0.019 | 0.929 ± 0.018 | | GPQA-D | DL7 | 0.916 ± 0.011 (n=594) | 0.939 ± 0.017 | 0.929 ± 0.018 | 0.919 ± 0.019 | 0.955 ± 0.015 | | GSM8k | off | 0.867 ± 0.009 (n=1319) | 0.856 ± 0.010 | 0.860 ± 0.010 | 0.864 ± 0.009 | 0.873 ± 0.009 | | GSM8k | DL7 | 0.863 ± 0.005 (n=5276) | 0.853 ± 0.010 | 0.854 ± 0.010 | 0.868 ± 0.009 | 0.865 ± 0.009 | | MRCR v2 | off | 0.282 ± 0.039 (n=100) | 0.334 ± 0.042 | 0.226 ± 0.036 | – | – | | MRCR v2 | DL7 | 0.343 ± 0.042 (n=100) | 0.339 ± 0.042 | 0.320 ± 0.042 | – | – | Sample counts: AIME25 n=60, GPQA-D n=198, GSM8k n=1319, MRCR n=100. Single MRCR runs swing by ~0.1 between repeats; a larger TP8 C8 matrix ({ours, stock} x {DCP on, off} x {spec off, DL7}, 750–900 samples per build) gives **0.296 (ours) vs 0.290 (stock)**.
Numerical validation and the MRCR output-length study - **Greedy logprobs, spec vs no-spec on the same build** (up to and including the first divergence): TP8 drift ≤ 0.50 vs stock's own 0.38, divergences only at near-ties (top-1/top-2 margin ≤ 0.50); TP8+DCP8 (~8k context) drift ≤ 0.38, margins ≤ 0.375, inside stock's B1-vs-B4 noise of 0.875. :heavy_check_mark: - **Greedy probes at 128k–256k context vs stock** (32 MRCR prompts, 4096 tokens, top-10 logprobs): every divergence is at an exact BF16 top-1/top-2 tie; ours-vs-stock |Δ logprob| (0.007–0.009, first divergence ~step 50–80) matches stock DCP-on vs DCP-off (0.014, ~59); no growth with position. Decode tok/s excludes prefill; output tok/s and TPOT include the other requests' 16k prefill chunks, so their gains are smaller. ## Details ### vLLM Integration No weight changes were made in this model implementation: it is fully compatible with Aggregated vLLM serving, and falls back to the default implementation for prefills, mixed batches, and large batches. The specialized decode runtime is implemented via _composition_: a SpecializedDecode object owned by the Kimi LLM model, built when supported (see `unsupported(...)`), and called during forward(). The runtime can opt-out of a batch (e.g. when it has too many tokens) by checking `decode.plan(...) is None`, and fall back to stock forward. I considered a few alternate designs but ultimately feel like this is the cleanest integration. It uses the ModelState protocol to build the runtime object and hook into initialize_kv_cache(). The rest of the integration is organized into subfolders, e.g. `vllm/models/kimi_k3/specialized_decode/nvidia/cutedsl/kda/` with the specialized implementation(s) for each component. ---

commits.pr_title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Split fused_wqa_wkv by token across TP ranks on SM90
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Without sequence parallelism, every TP rank computes DeepSeek-V4.1's `fused_wqa_wkv` (5120 → 1280 + 512) for all tokens, so all ranks do the same work. The checkpoint stores this weight as FP8 with UE8M0 block scales, which vLLM runs through its MXFP8 path. On SM90 that path is a W8A16 Marlin GEMM: on H20 it takes 1.79 ms per layer for an 8192-token prefill chunk, 72 ms per chunk over the 40 layers.

This PR splits the projection by token for batches of at least 2048 tokens. Each rank projects its token shard (`sp_shard`), and `sp_all_gather` rebuilds `qr_kv`. The change is confined to `DeepseekV4Attention._fused_wqa_wkv_gemm`:
- `_run_parallel_input_projections` is unchanged, so the multi-stream decision is the same as on main.
- The all-gather is issued on the current stream, right after the GEMM that produces its input.

`_shard_fused_wqa_wkv` in the NVIDIA decoder layer enables the split only when all of the following hold:
- **SM90.** On SM100, `fused_wqa_wkv` runs as a native MXFP8 GEMM, far cheaper than W8A16 Marlin, so the gather would be a much larger share of the cost. I have not measured SM100, and the H20 results below do not carry over to it.
- **No sequence parallelism.** There the hidden states are already sharded, and #57257 splits this projection for that case.
- **No LoRA.** The LoRA wrapper maps every token of the batch.
- **No micro-batching.** Two micro-batches would share the custom all-gather buffer.
- **No batch invariance.** Whether a token takes the split depends on the batch size.
- **The custom all-reduce is enabled and fully connected.** This serves only as a proxy for NVLink between all TP ranks. From 6144 tokens at TP8, the shard exceeds the custom all-gather's 2 MiB limit, so the gather itself runs on NCCL.

TP4 and TP2 take the same gate but were not measured. On Hopper they need pipeline parallelism to hold the checkpoint.

The compressor's `fused_wkv_wgate` and the indexer's `weights_proj` stay replicated, and `_run_parallel_input_projections`, which can run them on separate streams, is unchanged. They appear in only a few layers:
- the compressor in the 4 KV-source layers (2, 8, 14, 20);
- the indexer in the 8 index-source layers, which are those four plus 24, 28, 32 and 36.

At 8192 tokens, splitting them as well would save at most another 457 µs in a KV-source layer (last column of the second table; layer 20's compressor is half as wide). In the four indexer-only layers the projection is only 5120 → 32. This PR saves about 1.45 ms in each of the 40 layers, so it limits the split to this dominant projection.

**Why 2048 tokens.** On H20 the split is faster from 48 tokens (first table below). H100 and H200 have about 6.7 times H20's dense throughput with the same 900 GB/s NVLink, so the replicated GEMM costs much less there while the gather costs the same.

I have no H100 or H200 to measure on, so I scaled the H20 numbers pessimistically:
- a GEMM of 1024 rows or more runs 6.7 times faster than on H20;
- one of 512 rows runs 3.7 times faster, and one of 256 rows or fewer only twice as fast;
- the gather runs no faster.

Under these assumptions the break-even is about 1450 tokens, and 2048 is the next power of two. A measurement on H100 or H200 would confirm or retune it.

**Related work.** I found no upstream PR for the case without sequence parallelism. The fork commit bytedance-iaas/vllm@383776ac20 splits `fused_wqa_wkv` the same way, but behind an environment variable that is off by default, and not when speculative decoding is on.

## Test Plan

**Kernel benchmark.** Setup:
- Hardware: 8× H20 (SM90, 96 GB, NVLink), TP8.
- Software: torch 2.13.0+cu130, NCCL 2.29.7, vLLM nightly `0.30.1rc1.dev85+g8b84e1506` with this diff applied as a Python overlay.
- What it runs: `fused_wqa_wkv` is built as the model builds it, with random weights and the checkpoint's quantization, so SM90 runs Marlin. The second table times `_run_parallel_input_projections` from this branch, which calls `_fused_wqa_wkv_gemm`, with the model's projection shapes and three aux streams.

Timing follows `.agents/skills/kernel-microbenchmark`:
- One CUDA graph per candidate.
- Before every measured replay, an L2 flush (twice the L2 size) and a device-side barrier, both outside the timed interval.
- The time of a replay is the CUPTI span of its kernels. Each sample is the maximum over the 8 ranks, and the tables report the median of 50 samples.
- Candidates alternate within every round, and correctness is checked before timing.

The benchmark script is not part of this PR; I can add it under `benchmarks/kernels/` if that helps.

**Serving.** TP8 without expert parallelism. DSpark uses synthetic acceptance with a mean acceptance length of 3.51, the same distribution in both arms:

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --revision dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --language-model-only --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --max-model-len 262144 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 128 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":false}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.51,"enable_adaptive_verification":false}'
```

One `vllm bench serve` call per point:

| Point | ISL | OSL | C | N |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8K / 32K / 128K prompt TTFT | 8192 / 32768 / 131072 | 1 | 1 | 5 / 3 / 2 |
| 1K in / 1K out, C1 | 1024 | 1024 | 1 | 6 |
| 1K in / 1K out, C64 | 1024 | 1024 | 64 | 192 |
| 8K in / 1K out, C16 | 8192 | 1024 | 16 | 48 |
| 8K in / 1K out, C64 | 8192 | 1024 | 64 | 128 |

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend openai --endpoint /v1/completions --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len <ISL> --random-output-len <OSL> --random-range-ratio 0 --ignore-eos \
  --max-concurrency <C> --num-prompts <N> --num-warmups <C> --seed 1
```

Each arm ran on a fresh server, in the order this PR (B1), main (A1), main (A2), this PR (B2).

**Accuracy.** Full GSM8K (1,319 questions) through `/v1/chat/completions`, with real DSpark verification (`rejection_sample_method: block`) instead of synthetic acceptance:
- 5-shot multi-turn chat with thinking off (`chat_template_kwargs: {"thinking": false}`);
- temperature 0, seed 123, `max_tokens` 1024, 32 concurrent requests;
- each reply is scored by the number after `####`, or else by its last number.

## Test Result

**`fused_wqa_wkv`, split vs replicated** (µs per call, TP8, every batch size split so the crossover is visible):

| Tokens | Rows per rank | Replicated | Split + all-gather | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 6 | 1 | 14.1 | 23.2 | 0.61x |
| 12 | 2 | 14.6 | 23.1 | 0.63x |
| 24 | 3 | 19.2 | 21.1 | 0.91x |
| 48 | 6 | 25.9 | 20.3 | 1.28x |
| 96 | 12 | 49.6 | 21.5 | 2.31x |
| 384 | 48 | 99.7 | 35.8 | 2.78x |
| 1024 | 128 | 239.4 | 66.8 | 3.58x |

| 8192 | 1024 | 1794.7 | 346.9 | 5.17x |
| 16384 | 2048 | 3570.8 | 635.4 | 5.62x |

Up to 4096 tokens the gather is the custom all-reduce's all-gather; from 6144 tokens it is NCCL. From 4096 tokens on, the replicated Marlin GEMM runs at 83–84 TFLOPS.

**Input projections of one attention layer, main vs this PR** (µs; only this stage is timed, not the whole layer):

| Tokens | Layer without compressor or indexer (32 layers): main | This PR | Speedup | Layer with compressor and indexer (layers 2, 8, 14): main | This PR | Speedup | If compressor and indexer were also split |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1024 | 236.7 | 236.5 | same code | 337.6 | 337.7 | same code | 337.5 |
| 1536 | 351.1 | 348.8 | same code | 478.5 | 480.6 | same code | 481.1 |
| 2048 | 458.1 | 99.9 | 4.59x | 660.4 | 301.8 | 2.19x | 198.3 |

- **Estimate per 8K prefill chunk:** this stage gets about 1.45 ms faster in every layer, about 58 ms over the 40 layers. The serving results below are the measurement.
- **Correctness:** `qr_kv` differs from the replicated projection by at most 0.031 across two sweeps with different inputs. That is bf16 rounding from Marlin's M-dependent tiling. `kv_score` and `indexer_weights` are bitwise identical to main.

**Serving and accuracy.** The serving numbers are a sanity check with two servers per arm, not a precise measurement. Lower TTFT and higher output throughput are better, and Change compares the means of the two arms.
