commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Keep input_ids on later PP stages for raw-token models
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Model Runner V2 drops `input_ids` on every pipeline stage after the first, so models that set
`requires_raw_input_tokens` (they read token ids inside their decoder layers) cannot run with
`--pipeline-parallel-size > 1`. This keeps `input_ids` on later stages for those models, as Model Runner V1
already does. Fixes #55515.

## Claims

- MRV2 with pipeline parallelism works for models that set `requires_raw_input_tokens` (DeepSeek-V4 and V4.1
  vision variants, Qwen4Exp with N-gram PLE, Voxtral realtime): later stages receive `input_ids` in the execute
  path and in CUDA graph capture.
- Other models are unchanged: later stages still get `input_ids=None`.

## Validation

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4 x PP2 + EP, 8x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120), max-model-len 1M, CUDA graphs,
no speculative decoding. Same image both times; only the two files in this PR differ.

| | Startup | Smoke (25k- and 60k-token prompts) | Needle at 20/50/90% of a 22.5k-token prompt | ITL p50, bs1 / bs16 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| upstream main | fails: every PP rank 1 worker raises `ValueError: DeepSeek V4 vision MoE routing requires input_ids.` | – | – | – |
| this PR | serves (health OK after 250 s) | pass | 3/3 found | 11.1 / 17.7 ms per token |

<details><summary>Build and reproduction</summary>

Base: vLLM nightly image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-7d0b4e57aac4c4323225b0eee9ae960ce75ffffe` with FlashInfer
0.7.1 (for the sm_120 sparse-MLA decode shapes). DeepSeek-V4.1 on sm_120 with PP also needs fixes that are not on
main yet, so the validation build is our fork branch
[`quettaflop/vllm:sm120-dsv41-main`](https://github.com/quettaflop/vllm/tree/sm120-dsv41-main) on that commit. It
includes per-stage KV tensor placement (same fix as #60569) and 64-row sparse-MLA/indexer pages on sm_120 (same
issue as #60762 / #56509), plus other DeepSeek-V4.1 changes. Between the two runs only the two files in this PR
differ.

    vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --pipeline-parallel-size 2 \
      --enable-expert-parallel --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-seqs 64 --block-size 64 \
      --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41"}' \
      --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41

</details>

`pre-commit run` passes on the changed files. CI test: `test_distributed_oot_pp_raw_input_tokens` in
`tests/distributed/test_distributed_oot.py` serves a dummy OPT from the `vllm_add_dummy_model` plugin that sets
`requires_raw_input_tokens = True` and asserts `input_ids` is not None, with PP=2 on MRV2, eager and with CUDA
graphs, in the 2×L4 plugin step. Without the fix both cases fail on the PP rank 1 worker; reverting only the
`cudagraph_utils.py` change fails the CUDA-graph case during capture. It passes in
[Buildkite build 94033](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/94033). A dummy model is used because DeepSeek
V4/V4.1's sparse MLA kernels need sm90+ and the step runs on L4.

## Details

Root cause: `GPUModelRunner.execute_model` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`) and
`ModelCudaGraphManager.capture` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py`) set `model_inputs["input_ids"] = None`
on every non-first PP rank. Every rank still prepares the same input batch, so the ids are already in the input
buffer there; MRV1 passes them to all ranks (the text-only branch of `gpu_model_runner.py`). The new condition
reuses `requires_raw_input_tokens`, the check MRV2 already applies on the first rank when it passes
`inputs_embeds`.

Relation to open PRs: #55520 (DeepSeek V4) and #56444 (Qwen4Exp) relay `input_ids` through `IntermediateTensors`
per model, and #60234 forbids PLE layers on later ranks. This change fixes the runner once, with no extra
inter-stage transfer and no per-model code; the input_ids relays in those PRs become unnecessary, while their
other fixes (KV allocation, MTP drafter) are independent.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to prepare this change and this description; the commit carries a
`Co-authored-by` trailer.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Core] Uncount stop-trimmed spec tokens from num_computed_tokens
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

When a speculative decode step stops on an accepted draft (EOS, a stop token, or `max_tokens` reached before the bonus token), `_update_request_with_output` trims the step's later tokens, but `num_computed_tokens` keeps counting them. Rejections are rolled back in `update_from_output`; trimmed tokens are not.

Ordinary requests are freed right after the stop, so the count is never read again. A resumable (streaming-input) request continues: `_update_request_as_session` uses `num_computed_tokens` as the fold boundary, so the next chunk starts "already computed" over positions whose KV belongs to the trimmed drafts.

Prompt `[1, 2, 3]`, `max_tokens=2`, k=2. The prefill samples `10`; a step with drafts `[11, 12]` returns `[11, 12, 13]` (both accepted) and stops at `11`. Folding in the next chunk `[7, 8]`:

| | `all_token_ids` | `num_computed_tokens` | next step computes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main | `[1, 2, 3, 10, 11, 7, 8]` | 6 | `8` only; `7` reuses draft `12`'s KV |
| this PR | `[1, 2, 3, 10, 7, 8]` | 4 | `7, 8` |

The fix uncounts the trimmed tokens, so `num_computed_tokens` again covers all new tokens but the last kept one. The fold then drops that token exactly as it drops the final sampled token of a non-speculative turn, which is what makes a session's output identical with and without speculative decoding (see the GPU check below).

Under async scheduling the trimmed tokens' placeholders were never released either (`num_output_placeholders` was decremented by the post-trim count), so they are released too. `num_computed_tokens - num_output_placeholders` is unchanged, so neither the async `cache_blocks` frontier nor the `C - P` frontier from #58259 moves.

This count is also what stale block-hash truncation keys on (#52806, and the `del session.block_hashes[num_computed_tokens // hash_block_size:]` suggested on #58259): with the overshoot, the cut point lands too late and leaves stale hashes behind.

Diffusion schedulers inherit the change; resumable diffusion requests were not exercised.

## Not a duplicate

- #44526 clamps `num_computed_tokens` to `num_prompt_tokens` after the fold. That catches only an overshoot past the whole new chunk (`num_new_tokens <= 0`); in the example above it is a no-op and `7` is still skipped. This PR fixes the count where it goes wrong.
- #58259 (merged) fixed the async handoff race. Its `C - P` frontier also covers this case under async scheduling, but not under sync scheduling, where `num_output_placeholders` is always 0. This PR keeps `C - P` unchanged, so the two compose.
- #54979 caps its terminal `cache_blocks` call at `request.num_tokens` to work around the same overshoot; the cap stays correct.
- Searched open and closed PRs and issues for streaming input + speculative decoding, `num_computed_tokens` trimming, and `_update_request_as_session`; no other PR fixes this.

## Test Plan

```bash
# CPU
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py -q
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core tests/v1/streaming_input -q

# GPU (GB200)
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_streaming_input.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_async_scheduling.py::test_with_ngram_gpu_spec_decoding -v
```

New test: `test_next_chunk_fully_computed_after_stop_on_accepted_draft` (scheduler, sync and async scheduling): after the trimmed stop, the fold drops the last kept token and the next chunk is scheduled in full.

GPU check, run manually and not kept in CI: a 6-chunk streaming session (opt-125m, fp32 + FLEX_ATTENTION, greedy, `max_tokens=2` per chunk) must produce the same tokens and logprobs with and without ngram speculative decoding (k=4), with drafts accepted. The greedy tokens of this repetitive prompt do not change with the context, so logprobs are what catch the difference.

## Test Result

- Scheduler test: the sync case fails on main and passes with the fix. The async case passes on main since #58259 and is kept to check that this PR's `C`/`P` accounting still composes with it.
- `test_scheduler_streaming.py` + `test_scheduler.py` + `test_async_scheduler.py`: 221 passed.
- `tests/v1/core` + `tests/v1/streaming_input` (CPU): 797 passed. The 1 failure and 6 errors (`test_reset_prefix_cache_e2e`, `test_scheduler_e2e`) need a GPU and are identical on main.
- GPU on GB200:
  - Streaming session check, main: diverges from the second chunk on, e.g. logprobs `[-0.3593, -0.5455]` with ngram vs `[-0.3427, -0.7063]` without.
  - Streaming session check, this PR: tokens match and logprobs agree to ~1e-5; `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_streaming_input.py` passes.
  - Async spec-decode regression check (the placeholder accounting change applies to every async spec request, not only streaming): `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_async_scheduling.py::test_with_ngram_gpu_spec_decoding` passes, all 6 configs (sync/async, preemption, chunked prefill, mp/uni executor) match the non-speculative baseline in outputs and logprobs.
  - `ngram` is not yet supported by Model Runner V2, so the streaming session check uses the V1 model runner. The fix is in the scheduler and runner-independent. Async scheduling is covered by the scheduler test only.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to find, reproduce and fix this. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][HiSparse] Reuse pinned host pool after graph profiling
commits.pr_body:
HiSparse allocates and pins its host KV pool during profiling, then repeats that work for serving. Keep one engine-scoped pool, keyed by `instance_id`, and reuse its backing for the real KV cache.

Profiling teardown detaches temporary layer caches; connector shutdown or failed initialization releases the pool. This removes the per-layer ownership and preservation flags, leaving CUDA-graph teardown unchanged from main.

Adopts Matthew’s approach in [Etelis/vllm#9](https://github.com/Etelis/vllm/pull/9). Refs #60072; complements #60869.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm] Support DeepSeek-V4 hash routing in AITER Triton W4A16 MoE
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

#57867 rejects monolithic MoE kernels for hash-routed models, which disables the AITER Triton W4A16 backend for DeepSeek-V4. This adds a `_supports_hash_routing()` capability (default `False`), threads `input_ids`/`hash_indices_table` through `apply_monolithic`, and routes hash layers in `AiterW4A16ExpertsMonolithic` with aiter `routing_from_hash` (available in the pinned v0.1.24.post1).

Not a duplicate: #57478 only fuses the non-hash router gate. #58800 adds the same `_supports_hash_routing()` hook for its gfx1250-only W4A4 expert; this PR covers W4A16 (gfx950). Whichever lands second drops the shared `modular_kernel.py` hunk.

## Test

commits.pr_title: [Perf][MoE] Skip the TRTLLM fp8-block activation-scale transpose copy
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Skip the per-layer `a1q_scale.t().contiguous()` copy between per-token-group FP8 quantization and the FlashInfer TRTLLM fp8-block MoE experts by emitting the scales in the layout the experts consume. This is pure plumbing on top of the quant kernel's existing `column_major_scales` mode — no kernel changes. ~2% TPOT improvement at concurrency 4 on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 (TP4+EP).

## Claims

- Removes one `direct_copy_kernel` per MoE layer per decode step (24/step -> 0 on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) from the critical path.
- ~2% TPOT p50 improvement at concurrency 4 on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, TP4+EP on 4xGB300; parity at concurrency 1 (details below).
- Bitwise-identical expert inputs: the scale bytes are the same values, just allocated in the final physical layout, so there is no accuracy impact.
- Python-only change (+77/-14 across 5 files, mostly the test).

## Validation

### Correctness

- `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer.py`: 49 passed (+2 mxfp8 skips), including the new `transposed` arm of `test_trtllm_fp8_block_moe_deferred_finalize`, which builds the quant config through the production oracle + `no_dp_ep` path, asserts the prepared activation scale is column-major (`a1q_scale.t().is_contiguous()`), and asserts bitwise-equal expert output against the non-transposed baseline.
- No new test for the `column_major_scales` wrapper mode itself: it is a pre-existing feature already exercised by the CUTLASS/DeepGEMM/FlashInfer/PyTorch scaled-mm kernels on every CUDA run and by existing fusion/eplb tests.

### Profiler evidence

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, TP4+EP, decode step trace:

| | main | this PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `per_token_group_quant` launches / step | 24 | 24 |
| `direct_copy_kernel` launches / step | 24 | 0 |

### E2E perf

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, TP4+EP on 4xGB300, `vllm bench serve`, 2048 input / 256 output, `--ignore-eos`. main (`f46021a7fa`) and the branch (`9f75804588`) ran sequentially on the same node, two server instances each:

| Concurrency | main TPOT p50 (ms) | this PR TPOT p50 (ms) | Change |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 3.92-3.93 | parity (see below) | ~0% |
| 4 | 5.11-5.12 | 4.98-5.00 | -2.3% |

TPOT p99 at concurrency 4 improves from 5.67-6.04 ms to 5.57-5.58 ms. Concurrency-1 serve numbers were noisy across instances, so c=1 was A/B'd with interleaved `vllm bench latency` (bs=1, 2048/128): 0.756/0.704 s (this PR) vs 0.756/0.800 s (main) — no regression, as expected since the eliminated copies are nearly free inside a bs=1 CUDA graph.

## Details

- Root cause: the TRTLLM fp8-block kernels consume activation scales in the physical `[K/128, M]` (scale-major) layout, while the MoE per-token-group quant emits `[M, K/128]` row-major, so every layer paid a transpose copy between the quant kernel and the experts.
- The quant kernel's existing `column_major_scales=True` mode already allocates the scale buffer as a contiguous `[G, M]` tensor viewed as `[M, G]`, so on that buffer the experts' `.t().contiguous()` is a no-op returning the same tensor. The change just threads a new `FusedMoEQuantConfig.is_scale_transposed` flag — set by the fp8 oracle only for `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM` + `[128, 128]` blocks — through `no_dp_ep` into `moe_kernel_quantize_input`. TRTLLM expert code is unchanged.
- Scope: only `no_dp_ep` forwards the flag; dispatch-based paths (deepep, naive-dp, fi-nvl) keep row-major scales since their scales cross an all2all dispatch. Other MoE backends are unaffected.
- No accuracy eval: the scale bytes handed to the experts are bitwise-identical (same values, different physical layout), so outputs cannot change; the e2e runs above exercised the modified path at c=1-4.
- Duplicate-work check: nearest open PRs inspected — #59564 (value-only amax reduction inside the quant kernel, orthogonal), #53345 (deepep ep_scatter scale-stride bugfix), #44034 (XPU quant fallback); none touch the MoE activation-scale layout.

commits.pr_title: [MoE] Unify DeepGEMM MegaMoE experts behind one feature-matrix layer; add NVFP4
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Folds the three DeepGEMM MegaMoE expert implementations into one `DeepGemmMegaMoEExperts` layer. The three are DeepSeek V4/V4.1's `DeepseekV4MegaMoEExperts`, Kimi K3's `KimiK3MegaMoEExperts`, and the `DeepGemmMegaMoEBackend` pair under both. The new layer is driven by a feature matrix: routed precision × activation × fusable shared-expert precision. The PR also adds NVFP4 routed experts (DeepGEMM `nvfp4_mega_moe`) as a new row. It keeps the procedure from #60096: weights load straight into the DeepGEMM layout, with no post-load transform.

**Draft:** the end-to-end eval has not been run yet (see Validation).

## Claims

- **One layer.** Every DeepGEMM MegaMoE caller uses `forward(hidden_states, topk_weights, topk_ids, shared_experts=None)`.
- **Fusion decided at construction.** Fusion of the shared expert is decided once, from the shared MLP's weights, and never changes at runtime.
- **Supported matrix.** It covers every routed precision and activation that the pinned DeepGEMM exposes:

  | routed | kernel | dispatch | fusable shared | activations |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | mxfp4 | `fp8_fp4_mega_moe` (fp8xfp4) | MXFP8 | MXFP8 | swiglu, situ |
  | mxfp8 | `fp8_fp4_mega_moe` (fp8xfp8) | MXFP8 | MXFP8 | swiglu, situ |
  | nvfp4 | `nvfp4_mega_moe` | NVFP4, one scale per token | MXFP8, BF16 | swiglu |
  | bf16 | `bf16_mega_moe` | BF16 | BF16 | swiglu |

  `swiglu` takes optional `clamp`, `alpha` and `beta`. `situ` (Kimi K3) takes `alpha` and `beta`.
- **Existing models unchanged.** DeepSeek V4/V4.1 and Kimi K3 still build the MXFP4 row and pass the same kernel arguments as before. The mxfp8, nvfp4 and bf16 rows have no model caller yet.
- **Size.** Code under `vllm/` is +360 lines net. The refactor commit is −120, the NVFP4 commit is +472, and the two follow-up commits are −15 and +23.

## Validation

GB200 (SM100), vendored DeepGEMM at the current pin:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_deep_gemm_mega_moe.py \
    tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py \
    tests/model_executor/test_deep_gemm_warmup.py
# 138 passed in 67s
```

**Kernel numerics.** The real kernel is compared against an fp32 reference that runs on the same quantized weights and activations. The reference covers dispatch quantization, the activation, the L2 activation quantization and the shared expert. The metric is DeepGEMM's `calc_diff`; the test requires < 1e-3 and cosine > 0.99. The table shows the worst case over the activations each format supports:

| routed | unfused shared | fused MXFP8 shared | fused BF16 shared |
|---|---|---|---|
| mxfp4 | 2.9e-5 | 1.8e-4 | – |
| mxfp8 | 3.1e-5 | 1.8e-4 | – |
| nvfp4 | 1.8e-6 | 1.6e-4 | 1.4e-6 |
| bf16 | 2.1e-6 | – | 1.7e-6 |

**Negative controls.** Each of these deliberate breaks made the expected cases fail:

| break | cases that failed |
|---|---|
| wrong weight layout, activation or shared input (MX) | the affected cases |
| drop NVFP4 per-token `x_scales`, `l1_alpha` or `l2_alpha` | all 9 NVFP4 cases |
| drop the shared-expert input | all 6 fused cases |
| wrong shared `BLOCK_M` | the 3 fused-MXFP8 cases |

**Input staging.** The Triton staging kernels match DeepGEMM's reference quantizers (`per_token_cast_to_fp8`, `per_token_cast_to_nvfp4`) bit for bit. This covers values, scales, shared-expert inputs, unrouted padding and the zero-token case.

**Not yet done:**
- [ ] End-to-end DeepSeek-V4.1 gsm8k A/B against main: TP4, `--enable-expert-parallel`, `--kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}'`. The main baseline is 92.65% flexible / 92.57% strict.
- [ ] End-to-end Kimi K3 with `moe_backend=deep_gemm_mega_moe`.
- Only single-rank kernel numerics have been run; there is no multi-rank EP numerics test.

## Details

**Feature matrix.**
- Each `MegaMoEWeightFormat` row declares five things: the MMA type, the kernel entry point, the routed weight spec (dtype, packing, scale group, scale dtype), the dispatch quant key, and the fusable shared-expert specs.
- The layer validates its `MegaMoEActivation` against the row at construction.
- A new precision is a new row plus whatever staging it needs. It needs no new expert class.

**Shared-expert fusion.**
- The layer fuses the shared expert when two conditions hold. First, the shared MLP's weight dtype, scale dtype and shape match one of the row's shared specs. Second, the installed DeepGEMM exposes the shared-expert buffer and kernel API.
- Otherwise `forward` adds `shared_experts(hidden_states)` once.
- A fused layer raises if it is still handed a shared module.

**Input staging.**
- `prepare_megamoe.py` moved from `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/ops/` to `fused_moe/`. The old location caused an import cycle through `vllm.models.deepseek_v4`.
- It gained a BF16 passthrough and an NVFP4 kernel.
- Shared Triton helpers were factored out of the MX kernel, which is still bit-exact.

**NVFP4.**
- Dispatch quantizes hidden states with one NVFP4 scale per token, computed at runtime. The checkpoint's `w1`/`w3` `input_scale` are therefore unused. A model that wires NVFP4 must skip them.
- The kernel takes a single scalar L2 activation scale. The layer uses the largest `w2` `input_scale` across all experts. Every rank reads every expert's scale tensors during loading, so all ranks agree and EPLB expert moves stay valid.
- `l2_alpha` (the per-expert `w2` global scale × the L2 activation scale) is computed inside the staging kernel. This avoids an extra launch and stays correct after EPLB moves or a weight reload.
- The kernel takes one `l1_alpha` per expert, so the loader raises if `w1` and `w3` `weight_scale_2` differ (relative tolerance 1e-5, as in ModelOpt's `allclose` check). It compares the two shards of the same load, not the live slot, so a reload that changes the scale does not trip it. ModelOpt's and Quark's NVFP4 MoE only warn here; they also use one scale.
- Meta tensors, which reload dry runs pass, skip this host-side scale state.
- The L2 activation scale is a host scalar in DeepGEMM's API, so CUDA graphs capture its value. A weight reload that changes the `w2` input scales needs a graph recapture. In eager mode the layer recomputes the max on reload. Passing it as a device tensor needs a DeepGEMM change and a pin bump, so it is left for a follow-up.

**Behaviour changes for existing models:**
- DeepSeek V4/V4.1 now also run Kimi K3's one-time first-launch barrier: a device sync plus a gloo barrier on the EP CPU group. It runs on the first forward, which is the eager profile run before graph capture.
- `get_deep_gemm_mega_moe_backend()` and the backend classes are removed. Their docstring named them as the override point for plugins and SM90. The extension point is now a new `MegaMoEWeightFormat` row, plus `check_deep_gemm_mega_moe_supported`.

**CI.** The new test file and the moved sources are added to the B200 "DeepSeek V4 Kernels" step. Before this PR the SM100 numerics ran only from `tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py`. The staging-kernel tests are gated to SM100, where those kernels run. The L4 "MoE Kernels" shards also collect `tests/kernels/moe/`, and on SM89 Triton casts fp32 to fp8 through fp16 (`cvt.rz.f16.f32`). That rounds the NVFP4 block scales twice, so the bit-exact test failed there. The loader and fusion-selection tests in the file still run on L4.

**Unchanged:** the XPU `DeepseekV4MegaMoEExperts`, which uses a different kernel.

**Related PRs:**
- Not a duplicate: no open PR unifies the MegaMoE expert classes or wires `nvfp4_mega_moe`.
- #60096 (merged): the load-into-kernel-layout procedure this PR keeps.
- #60895 (GLM-5.3 block-FP8 MegaMoE): edits the backend classes this PR removes, so the two conflict. After this PR lands it fits the mxfp8 row, plus a load-time block-scale requant.
- #59003 (weight reload for packed MegaMoE buffers): also targets the removed classes. #60096 already writes checkpoint shards in place.
- #53556 (Kimi K3 BF16 shared-expert fusion into the latent tail) and #40833 (modular-kernel MegaMoE integration, stale draft) take different approaches.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Make Humming DeviceInfo lookups traceable under torch.compile
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes vllm-project/humming#147 for vLLM: models served through Humming fail torch.compile with `RecursionError` whenever Humming's forward path quantizes or Hadamard-transforms activations (seen during warmup of MXFP4 MoE checkpoints on H200). This patches Humming from the `vllm.utils.humming` facade so the pinned `humming-kernels==0.1.17` works for v0.32.0.

## Claims

- torch.compile (`fullgraph=True`) works again on Humming forward paths that run `may_process_input` (input quantization, Hadamard): no `RecursionError`, no Dynamo `Unsupported`.
- Works with the currently pinned humming 0.1.17. The upstream fix (vllm-project/humming#148, in the upcoming 0.1.18) is **not sufficient on its own** for vLLM (see Details).
- No behavior change in eager mode, apart from no longer re-querying device properties on every forward call.

## Validation

B300 (SM103), this branch on main with `humming-kernels[cu13]==0.1.17`:

| Check | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| New `tests/quantization/test_humming_compile.py` | `RecursionError` | passed |
| E2E: Qwen3-0.6B, `--quantization humming`, int6 weights + Hadamard + int8 activations, torch.compile + CUDA graphs | `RecursionError` at engine init | correct output ("Paris, and the capital of Italy is Rome…") |
| Same E2E with only the #148 `__getattr__` fix backported (on 0.1.16) | — | `torch._dynamo.exc.Unsupported` on `_DeviceInfo.__new__` |
| Standalone repro from humming#147 (`copy.copy`, `torch.compile`, `fullgraph=True`) | `RecursionError` | OK |

```bash
VLLM_HUMMING_ONLINE_QUANT_CONFIG='{"dtype":"int6","hadamard_block_size":-1}' \
VLLM_HUMMING_INPUT_QUANT_CONFIG='{"dtype":"int8"}' \
  python -c 'from vllm import LLM; print(LLM("Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", quantization="humming").generate("The capital of France is"))'
```

Regression tests (same setup): `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py tests/kernels/core/test_activation.py tests/quantization/test_humming_ignore.py tests/quantization/test_humming_mxfp4_block_fp8.py tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp4_kernel_selection.py tests/model_executor/test_utils.py -k humming` → 194 passed.

Not run locally on Hopper. The new test runs in the H200 Quantization CI step, and I added `vllm/utils/humming.py` to that step's trigger paths. Note the existing Humming lm-eval configs all use `--enforce-eager`, which is why CI never caught this.

## Details

**Root cause.** On every call, `LayerConfig.check_device` and the PDL heuristics (`_resolve_use_pdl` → `get_heuristics_class`) build a new `humming.device.DeviceInfo(device)`. vLLM traces these from `may_process_input` inside its fullgraph-compiled region. Two problems stack up:
1. `DeviceInfo` has `__slots__` and a catch-all `__getattr__`. When Dynamo creates the instance, it reads the unset `_value` slot, which re-enters `__getattr__` and recurses forever. humming#148 fixes this by raising `AttributeError` for private names.
2. With (1) fixed, Dynamo still can't trace the pybind `_DeviceInfo(index)` constructor, so fullgraph compile fails with `Unsupported`. Reading attributes from an extension object that already exists does trace fine; that's why the module-global `current_device` already works under compile. Humming main still has these per-call constructions, so 0.1.18 alone would still break vLLM.

**Fix.** On first use of the facade, `_patch_humming()`:
- backports the #148 `__getattr__` change (also fixes `copy.copy(DeviceInfo)`), and
- replaces the `DeviceInfo` name in the five Humming modules that call it (`config.config`, `transform`, `tune`, `tune.process_input`, `utils.smem`) with a factory that returns one cached instance per device index. `prepare_layer_config` populates the cache eagerly during weight processing, so at trace time Dynamo only sees a dict lookup on an existing object.

All vLLM Humming access goes through the lazy facade, so the patch is always applied before any layer is prepared. The swap is skipped for any module whose `DeviceInfo` is no longer Humming's class. `DeviceInfo` only exposes static device properties, so caching it is safe.

**Follow-up.** This should be removed once Humming's `DeviceInfo` can be constructed in traced code (for example, by caching inside Humming itself); there's a TODO. I'll raise this on the Humming side so 0.1.18+ can drop the patch.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] Route softmax MoE top-k, including fused shared-expert sigmoid, through AITER topk_gating
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On ROCm, softmax MoE routing uses AITER's legacy `topkGatingSoftmax` launcher. This routes `FusedTopKRouter` and the fused-shared-expert router (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1`) through `aiter.ops.topk.topk_gating` instead, which keeps selected-mass renormalization in-kernel (ROCm/aiter#4460), has the E=512 `prefill_n` dispatch (ROCm/aiter#5334), and with ROCm/aiter#6306 scores the shared-expert columns with sigmoid in the same launch. `dispatch_topk_softmax_func` decides per launch between `topk_gating` and the legacy `topk_softmax`. This PR makes the selection the default on CDNA3 and CDNA4 (gfx942, gfx950); every other architecture keeps the legacy launcher. gfx950 is the main sweep; gfx942 (MI300-class) was verified more lightly (see the gfx942 section). The blast radius is implicitly limited to Qwens, because based on my search other models won't use the `topk_gating`.

Not a duplicate: searched open PRs for `topk_gating` and `aiter topk softmax`; no other PR routes softmax top-k through `topk_gating`. #57246 fixes the eager `torch.topk` fallback in `fused_topk_bias`, and #55147 fixes the width of the `topk_ids` buffer AITER's kernels write; neither changes which AITER launcher is used.

## Claims

- On the same nightly, with only this PR and ROCm/aiter#6306 added, `topk_gating` is **+0.7% to +1.5% output-throughput geomean per cell** for Flash-Next (E=512, top-10, one shared expert) at TP2 with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS` 1 and 0, at three `max-num-batched-tokens` (2048, 4096, 8192), and **+1.3% to +1.9%** for Qwen3-30B-A3B (E=128, top-8) at TP1 in two passes per cell, over the four rows that repeat. Single-stream decode (1k/1k, concurrency 1) is the largest effect: +2.0% to +4.4% in every cell.
- Kernel: for E=512 / top-10 with one shared expert, `topk_gating` is 37–47% faster than `topk_softmax(..., "sigmoid")` at T ≤ 1024 and level at T = 2048–4096 (AITER op test, table below).
- No directional accuracy change: GSM8K on all 9 cells, paired, 134 problems fixed and 126 broken in total (net +8 of 11,871), no cell below p = 0.12. The six cells of the Qwen3-30B rerun are also consistent with noise (no cell below p = 0.39).
- gfx942 (MI300-class): the kernel passes AITER's op test and the vLLM unit tests there with zero routing mismatches, is neutral to slightly positive end to end (+2.0% and +0.45% output-throughput geomean on Qwen3-30B at mbt 4096 and 2048; +1.4% to +4.7% on three Flash-Next-FP8 TP2 rows), and GSM8K is unchanged (no cell below p = 0.16). This is a lighter check than the gfx950 sweep; details below.
- Which launches change: on CDNA3 and CDNA4 (gfx942, gfx950), contiguous gating rows with T ≤ 4096 tokens, and shared experts only with sigmoid scoring and 1, 2, 4 or 8 shared experts. Everything else, and every other GPU architecture, keeps `topk_softmax`. **There is no env var to turn it on/off.**

## Validation

**Unit tests.** On one MI355X, in the candidate image (below):

```bash
pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_topk.py tests/model_executor/test_enabled_custom_ops.py -k topk
# 74 passed, 19 deselected   (at b4c61b0e0)
pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_topk.py tests/model_executor/test_enabled_custom_ops.py
# 93 passed
```

On gfx942 (MI300-class), on the nightly base with this PR's net diff and the gate change applied: 35 passed in `test_enabled_custom_ops.py -k topk` and 39 in `test_rocm_aiter_topk.py`.

`tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_topk.py` checks the shared-expert suffix against a torch reference; `test_topk_softmax_dispatch_aiter_topk_gating` pins which launcher each launch shape takes, on the enabled architectures and (monkeypatched) on another one: shared-expert sigmoid with 1/2/4/8 shared experts, an unsupported count, wrong or missing shared scoring, mismatched row strides, a narrow weights buffer, non-contiguous rows, T = 4096 versus 4097, and the kill switch (each launch shape on gfx950 and elsewhere).

**Kernel evidence.** `op_tests/test_moe_topk_gating.py` from ROCm/aiter#6306, MI355X, E=512, top-10, bf16, renorm, one shared expert. Mean kernel time per call, one run, lower is better. Every case has 0 routing mismatches against a torch reference.

| T | `topk_gating` (µs) | legacy `topk_softmax` (µs) | Δ |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 5.56 | 9.76 | −43% |
| 16 | 5.87 | 10.51 | −44% |
| 64 | 5.86 | 10.86 | −46% |
| 256 | 6.05 | 11.42 | −47% |
| 1024 | 6.56 | 10.42 | −37% |
| 2048 | 10.66 | 10.60 | +0.5% |
| 4096 | 12.84 | 13.14 | −2.3% |

Above T = 1024 the kernel runs its shared-memory fallback, which is level with the legacy launcher; above T = 4096 vLLM keeps the legacy launcher (`_AITER_TOPK_GATING_MAX_TOKENS`), where an earlier measurement had `topk_gating` losing at 8K-token prefill chunks.

**End to end.** MI355X (gfx950). Both arms are the same image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-81198e97ba7eee2a22540caaa756b7fdddcb4d93`; the candidate adds only this PR's vLLM diff. Server flags in both arms: `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, `--max-num-seqs 256`, `--no-enable-prefix-caching`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9`, `--trust-remote-code`, thinking off, and `--max-num-batched-tokens` as in the column. It was verified that every candidate server loaded `module_moe_topk`; no control server did. Router `T` is the decode concurrency in decode rows and `min(mbt, prompt)` per prefill chunk, so prefill chunks at mbt 8192 take the legacy launcher in both arms.

Flash-Next is `amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4` at TP2 (`--max-model-len 262144 --reasoning-parser qwen3`). Qwen3-30B-A3B is `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B` (bf16) at TP1.

**Qwen3-30B-A3B, TP1.** Two passes per cell, with the control and candidate cards swapped between passes. Output tok/s, candidate vs control, pass 1 / pass 2 (higher is better).

```bash
  --max-model-len 262144 --reasoning-parser qwen3 --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --trust-remote-code \
  --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}'

python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend vllm --dataset-name random --request-rate inf \
  --random-range-ratio 1.0 --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --max-concurrency 32 --num-prompts 128 --warmup-requests 32 --seed 302

lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args model=amd/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Quark-MXFP4,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=32,timeout=1200,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False,max_gen_toks=2048 \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --apply_chat_template --batch_size 32 --seed 4321 --log_samples

pytest -q tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_topk.py tests/model_executor/test_enabled_custom_ops.py -k topk
```

The other rows use `--random-input-len/--random-output-len/--max-concurrency/--num-prompts/--warmup-requests/--seed` of 1024/1024/1/8/1/301, 1024/1024/128/256/128/303, 8192/128/8/32/8/304, 8192/1024/32/64/32/305 and 16384/128/2/8/2/306.

## Details

**What runs before and after.** Before, every softmax top-k on ROCm with AITER (`FusedTopKRouter`, and the fused-shared-expert router) ran `topk_softmax`, AITER's legacy launcher. After, `dispatch_topk_softmax_func` takes the launch's tensors and shared-expert arguments and returns `rocm_aiter_ops.topk_gating` on CDNA3 and CDNA4 (gfx942, gfx950) when `_aiter_topk_gating_supported` accepts the launch, and `topk_softmax` otherwise (including on every other architecture). `_aiter_topk_gating_supported` accepts contiguous gating rows with at most 4096 tokens; with shared experts it also needs sigmoid scoring, 1, 2, 4 or 8 of them, `topk_weights` and `topk_indices` sharing a row stride, and `topk_weights` wide enough for the shared columns. The shared-expert ids stay as the caller prefilled them, as with the legacy launcher. `_rocm_aiter_topk_gating_impl` is a plain call into `aiter.ops.topk.topk_gating`; the router runs inside the opaque `moe_forward` custom op, so nothing here changes graph capture.

**Why the 4096-token cap.** At E=512 / top-10 the kernel is level with the legacy launcher at T = 2048 and 4096 and was slower at 8K-token prefill chunks in an earlier measurement, so above 4096 the legacy launcher keeps serving. The cap is a named constant in the router, not a magic number.

**Why no env var.** The sweep shows a small positive effect at every shape tested on gfx950 and no reproducible loss, so there is nothing to opt into, and the path is the default under the existing AITER enablement (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER`, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE`) on gfx942 and gfx950. gfx942 was verified more lightly than gfx950 (see the gfx942 section); the gate is one line (`is_topk_gating_enabled`), so another architecture can be added the same way once it is measured.

commits.pr_title: [MoE] Shape-based padding for FlashInfer TRT-LLM MXFP8 experts (gated and non-gated)
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The FlashInfer TRT-LLM MXFP8 MoE kernel needs `intermediate % 128 == 0` and `hidden % 256 == 0`; otherwise it fails with `No valid config found`. This PR pads MXFP8 experts by shape on that backend, for gated and non-gated experts alike, so MXFP8-MoE checkpoints with misaligned expert sizes can run.

## Claims

- MXFP8 MoE layers with misaligned intermediate or hidden sizes now run on `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM`, gated or not.
- Aligned models are unchanged: no copy and no runtime padding.
- A W4A4 checkpoint with an MXFP8 MoE that this enables reaches **1.71×** the output tok/s/GPU of the BF16 model on GB300 at concurrency 64.

## Validation

- Unit tests: `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer.py -k mxfp8` gives 14 passed on B200. That is the new test (gated SiLU and non-gated ReLU², aligned and misaligned shapes such as 1856×2688, against `fused_experts` on the dequantized weights) plus the 4 existing MXFP8 TRT-LLM tests.

```bash
vllm serve $MODEL --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --max-num-seqs 128 --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 --max-model-len 32768 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --trust-remote-code --async-scheduling --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2,"moe_backend":"flashinfer_trtllm"}' \
  --mamba-cache-mode none --mamba-backend flashinfer --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float16 \
  --enable-mamba-cache-stochastic-rounding --mamba-cache-philox-rounds 5 --use-replayssm \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","max_cudagraph_capture_size":32768}'
```

- Accuracy (GB300): GPQA-diamond through NeMo Gym on 1x GB300, TP1, MTP=2 (198 questions x 8 repeats, thinking on, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95), served as above plus
  `--max-model-len 262144 --reasoning-parser nemotron_v3`. pass@1 (mean over the 8 repeats ±
  standard error) is 76.45 ± 0.70% without prefix reuse and 76.58 ± 0.45% with prefix reuse
  (`--enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align`, no ReplaySSM).
- Perf (GB300, TP1, speed-bench 1k prompts / OSL 200, no spec decode, same serve flags otherwise, concurrency 64): the W4A4 + MXFP8-MoE checkpoint reaches **9,640 output tok/s/GPU** (189.6 tok/s/user) vs BF16 5,648 (101.2), i.e. 1.71× throughput and 1.87× per user.
- `pre-commit run --files` on the changed files passes, including mypy.

## Details

- New `align_mxfp8_moe_weights_for_fi_trtllm`, next to `align_moe_weights_for_fi`:
  - It reuses `align_moe_weights_for_fi` for the intermediate size, padding gate and up halves separately.
  - It pads the hidden size with zero weights, and pads the UE8M0 scales the same way with 127 (scale 1.0).
- `prepare_fp8_moe_layer_for_fi` calls it on the MXFP8 TRT-LLM path and sets `intermediate_size_per_partition` and `hidden_dim` at the call site. The MoE runner then pads the activations to the padded hidden size and crops the output.
- The test uses `TrtLlmFp8ExpertsMonolithic`. `TrtLlmFp8ExpertsModular` (`trtllm_fp8_block_scale_routed_moe`) never passes `activation_type`, so it always runs the kernel gated.

commits.pr_title: [Spec Decode] Don't reserve DFlash/DSpark draft slots in the scheduler token budget
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

DFlash and DSpark reserve `max_num_new_slots_for_drafting` draft slots per request in the scheduler token budget (K for DFlash, K − 1 for DSpark), but neither drafts in the target batch. This PR sets those slots to 0 and instead caps running requests (`max_num_active_seqs`) at `max_num_batched_tokens // num_lookahead_tokens`, so the separate draft pass still fits its buffers. Fixes #52922.

## Claims

- DFlash/DSpark requests no longer pay for draft slots. A DSpark decode with K = 5 is charged 6 tokens instead of 10. With `--max-num-batched-tokens 512` that raises running requests from 52 to 64 and output throughput from 1373 to 3390 tok/s (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark on GB300, table below).
- The draft pass stays within its `max_num_batched_tokens`-row buffers. A request cap does this instead of the slots, and it only binds when `max_num_seqs × num_lookahead_tokens > max_num_batched_tokens`.
- This applies to DFlash on both model runners and to DSpark (MRV2-only), through the shared scheduler config. Slot accounting for P-EAGLE, PARD and draft models is unchanged.

## Validation

**Unit tests**, this revision (rebased on f26d9f432c), one GB300 node:

```bash
pytest tests/test_config.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_causality.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_lookahead.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_profile.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dspark_topk.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_warmup_blocks.py
```

- Result: 1137 passed, 5 skipped (ROCm-only), 1 failed. The failure, `test_is_encoder_decoder[meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-False]`, needs a gated repo and fails on `main` too.
- New test `test_block_drafters_cap_requests_instead_of_draft_slots`, for DFlash and anchor-sampling DSpark, checks that admission stops at `max_num_batched_tokens // num_lookahead_tokens` and that admitted prompts are scheduled in full. It fails if the cap is removed or main's draft-slot charges return, and the DSpark case fails if the cap divides by K + 1.
- pre-commit passes, including mypy.

**End to end**, this PR against `main` (f26d9f432c), same build and node:
- Setup: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark (K = 5), TP4 on one GB300, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve ... --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 512 --no-enable-prefix-caching`.
- Load: `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 256 --random-output-len 1536 --random-range-ratio 0.33 --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --max-concurrency 128 --num-prompts 512 --seed 0`, with `vllm:num_requests_running` scraped every 2 s. One run per side.

| `--max-num-batched-tokens 512` | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Max running requests | 52 | 64 |
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 1373 | 3390 |
| TPOT p50 / p99 (ms) | 29.2 / 63.5 | 15.7 / 36.0 |
| TTFT p50, incl. queueing (s) | 93.6 | 30.0 |
| Acceptance length | 4.72 | 4.73 |

- Variability: the previous revision, measured the same way with 2048 prompts and two interleaved runs per side, gave 51 vs 64 running and 1354 vs 3448 tok/s, within 2% of these numbers.
- With `--max-num-seqs 128`, this PR runs up to 85 requests (2167 tok/s). The request cap is 102 (512 // 5) and does not bind: each decode schedules 1 + K = 6 tokens, so the 512-token budget fills at 85.
- With the default budget, greedy outputs for 20 fixed prompts are byte-identical between `main` and this PR (3197 completion tokens).
- Measured on 299173db51. This revision moves the cap into `VllmConfig` and merges the startup check without changing admission: for this setup, its engine config leaves `max_num_active_seqs` unset at `--max-num-seqs 64` and lowers it to 102 at `--max-num-seqs 128`.
- Not run: DFlash end to end on either runner.

## Details

- **Root cause.** Both drafters run a separate fixed-width query pass. Context KV is precomputed from the target's hidden states into its own buffers, and each request's query rows go into buffers of `max_num_batched_tokens` rows: `DFlashSpeculator`/`DSparkSpeculator` on MRV2, `DFlashProposer.input_ids` on MRV1. The slots only enforced `num_reqs × query rows ≤ max_num_batched_tokens`. A request cap gives the same bound without spending target budget.
- **Why throughput gains more than 64/52.** On main, the 2–32 tokens left over split each new prefill into small chunks. Most steps then mix prefill into the decode batch and miss the FULL decode CUDA graph: ITL p50 is 169 ms on main vs 30 ms here.
- **Divisor.** `num_lookahead_tokens` equals the draft pass's query rows per request: K for anchor-sampling DSpark, K + 1 for DFlash and fill-in DSpark. Each query row writes KV at a position that `allocate_slots(num_lookahead_tokens=...)` must cover. So it cannot fall below the query width without breaking draft KV allocation, and if it grows the cap only tightens. This also covers fill-in DSpark, whose old K − 1 charge did not bound its K + 1 query rows.
- **Where the cap lives.** Right after the startup check, `VllmConfig` lowers `scheduler_config.max_num_active_seqs` to the cap only when the cap is below the current limit, and logs why, e.g. `The dspark draft pass needs 5 query tokens per request within max_num_batched_tokens=512. Overriding max_num_active_seqs from 128 to 102.` The scheduler is unchanged. Only its admission check reads `max_num_active_seqs`; unlike `max_num_seqs`, it doesn't size runner buffers or CUDA graphs and isn't part of the config hash.
- **Startup check.** The existing `max_num_batched_tokens` check in `VllmConfig` now compares against `num_lookahead_tokens` instead of the draft slots. `num_lookahead_tokens` is at least every method's slots and covers the DFlash/DSpark draft pass, so the check still rejects a budget too small for one request's draft pass. It is slightly stricter than before: EAGLE, MTP and draft models now need a budget above K, and DFlash above K + 1, far below any practical budget.
- **MRV1.** DSpark is MRV2-only. MRV1 DFlash shares the scheduler and its drafter has the same structure, so it gets the same change. It is covered by unit tests only, not end to end.
- **Review changes.** Following @TheEpicDolphin's review:
  - the fix moved into `max_num_new_slots_for_drafting`, and the cap now applies on both runners instead of only MRV2;
  - the cap divides by `num_lookahead_tokens`, so anchor-sampling DSpark uses K rather than K + 1.
- **Not a duplicate.**
  - #53080 (open, conflicting) replaces `max_num_new_slots_for_drafting` with a per-step draft budget for every method (+237/−77).
  - #52996 (open, conflicting) adds a DSpark-only budget charged K per request, which leaves DFlash over-charged.
  - #53970 resizes the drafter buffers; it is complementary.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the change, the tests, the test runs and this description.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Fix Apertus streaming scientific notation
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix corrupted scientific-notation arguments in Apertus streaming tool calls.

## Details

The parser could emit incomplete numbers before receiving their exponents. Since streamed arguments cannot be retracted, a value such as `-2e-3` could produce invalid arguments like `-20.002`.

Exclude `Allow.NUM` during incremental parsing to avoid emitting incomplete numeric values. Final parsing and incremental string streaming remain unchanged.

Numbers may be delayed until a terminating delimiter arrives.

## Validation

Added three regression cases covering positive and negative exponents, including numbers inside arrays.

- Before: **3 failed**.
- After: **22 passed** in the Apertus parser suite.
- All applicable pre-commit checks passed, including Ruff, mypy, and test coverage checks.

```bash
  tests/tool_parsers/test_apertus_tool_parser.py -q

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/tool_parsers/apertus_tool_parser.py \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_apertus_tool_parser.py
```

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Preserve streaming chunk boundaries in RequestOutputCollector
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

**Bug:** `RequestOutputCollector` (`vllm/v1/engine/output_processor.py`) keeps a single `self.output` slot and merges DELTA outputs into it when the producer runs ahead of the consumer. `RequestOutput.add()` overwrites `finish_reason`, so for streaming-input (resumable) sessions the per-chunk boundary marker (a `finish_reason` on a non-finished output) is erased when a merge spans a chunk boundary — the consumer sees two chunks' replies glued together.

**Fix:** `RequestOutputCollector` keeps its original single-slot merging. A new `StreamingInputOutputCollector` subclass, constructed only by `_add_streaming_input_request` (`vllm/v1/engine/async_llm.py`), adds a `_backlog` deque: while the slot or the backlog tail carries a chunk boundary, incoming outputs are queued into / merged within the backlog instead of being merged into the boundary output, and `get`/`get_nowait` promote backlog entries into the slot in FIFO order. Exceptions remain terminal (they clear the backlog and take over the slot). Non-streaming requests use the base collector and are unaffected.

## Why this is not duplicate work

This PR is bug 1 of 4 split out of #53861 so the collector fix can be reviewed and merged independently; the original author of #53861 (Benedikt Falk) is credited via `Co-authored-by`. Bugs 2+3 of #53861 are split into #58942; bug 4 remains in #53861.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py -q -k collector
pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/engine/output_processor.py vllm/v1/engine/async_llm.py tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py
```

## Test Result

- Collector tests: `3 passed, 50 deselected` — including `test_streaming_input_collector_preserves_chunk_boundary`, which exercises the new subclass. Bug-guard verified: replaying the same output sequence through the base `RequestOutputCollector` erases the boundary (`finish_reason` becomes `None`, token_ids from two chunks glued together).
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` / `mypy` (pre-commit hook): pass.
- A full-file pytest run on this Mac is blocked by two pre-existing environment issues unrelated to this change: a segfault in `tests/conftest.py` `cleanup_fixture` → `torch.accelerator.empty_host_cache` (reproduces on unmodified `main`; bypassed locally via the repo's `skip_global_cleanup` marker) and 401 gated-repo errors fetching `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B` from HuggingFace (tokenizer-dependent tests). The 19 non-tokenizer tests pass.

## AI assistance

This change was prepared with AI assistance (Kimi Code CLI); the human submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Reject Cohere REQUIRED tool choice without tools
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Reject Cohere Chat v2 requests that select `tool_choice="REQUIRED"` without a nonempty tools list, as required by the [Cohere specification](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/chat). Both chat and render endpoints now return a Cohere-shaped HTTP 400 before downstream processing.

## Claims

- Reject omitted, null and empty `tools` when tool choice is REQUIRED.
- Preserve valid required-tool requests and existing behavior for NONE or unspecified tool choice.

## Validation

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/cohere/test_protocol.py \
  tests/entrypoints/cohere/test_api_router.py \
  tests/entrypoints/cohere/test_serving_conversion.py \
  --confcutdir=tests/entrypoints/cohere -q

git diff --check
```

- **172 passed** on upstream base `9cede34a6`, including 7 new regression/compatibility scenarios.
- HTTP tests exercise the real routes, vLLM exception handlers and Cohere error-envelope middleware without an engine. They verify rejection before either handler is reached. Existing conversion tests cover valid REQUIRED requests with tools.
- Ruff lint and format checks passed for the three changed Python files; `git diff --check` passed. Existing Buildkite entrypoint jobs run the Cohere test directory.
- Validation runs on CPU without model weights and covers request parsing, HTTP error handling and conversion. No model-generation or accuracy evaluation was run.

## Details

The Cohere request model checks the tool-choice enum but lacks cross-field validation. Conversion constructs a shared `ChatCompletionRequest` before assigning tools and tool choice, bypassing its construction-time invariant. With no tools, rendering parameters then discard the requested tool choice. Add the check to the Cohere request model using the existing `VLLMValidationError` path.

Minimal baseline reproduction, without model weights:

```python
from vllm.entrypoints.cohere.protocol import CohereChatV2Request

CohereChatV2Request(
    model="m",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Use a tool."}],
    tool_choice="REQUIRED",
)
```

Upstream `9cede34a6` accepts this input, converts the choice to `"required"`, and then produces rendering parameters with `tool_choice=None`. This change raises `VLLMValidationError(parameter="tool_choice")` during request parsing. The same before/after behavior was verified for explicit null and empty tools.

Searches of open, closed and merged PRs on 2026-10-15 found no matching fix. Related [#52467](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52467) standardizes existing validation errors, [#60309](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60309) maps handler exceptions to client error responses, and [#60586](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60586) fixes JSON-schema forwarding; none adds this cross-field validation.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Skip exited descendants when finding the worker in the FT e2e test
commits.pr_body:
Failed CI: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/94610/list?sid=01a1373d-e190-4447-8cf4-9e6e4180d658&tab=output

_kill_worker_process lists every descendant of the API server and calls cmdline() on each to find the worker. With psutil >= 6 (CI pins 6.1.0), cmdline() raises ZombieProcess for a process that exited but was never reaped, and NoSuchProcess for one reaped mid-scan. One exited helper anywhere in the tree therefore failed the test before any fault was injected.

This happened on every fault-tolerance-e2e-2xh100 run built with the DeepGEMM pin from #59482 (builds 94501, 94505, 94523, 94591, 94610). At import, DeepGEMM starts an MLOPart helper (python3) from each worker; on H100 it exits at once and is never waited on. #61510 reverted that pin, but the test should not depend on every descendant being alive.

Original issue:
```
  >                       raise original_exception
  E                       psutil.ZombieProcess: PID still exists but it's a zombie (pid=8695)
  utils.py:1829: ZombieProcess
  ======================================================================= warnings summary =======================================================================
  <frozen importlib._bootstrap>:488
    <frozen importlib._bootstrap>:488: DeprecationWarning: builtin type SwigPyPacked has no __module__ attribute
  <frozen importlib._bootstrap>:488
    <frozen importlib._bootstrap>:488: DeprecationWarning: builtin type SwigPyObject has no __module__ attribute
```
Skip such descendants. A dead worker still fails the assert.

commits.pr_title: [Core] Apply prefill_schedule_interval outside data parallelism
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`prefill_schedule_interval` defers new prefills to every Nth engine step, so that decode
runs in longer uninterrupted stretches instead of meeting prefill on most steps. Today it
only takes effect under data parallelism: `DPEngineCoreProc._should_throttle_prefills()`
drives the cadence from a `step_counter` shared across ranks, while the base
`EngineCore._should_throttle_prefills()` returns `False` unconditionally. Setting the
option on a single engine is silently a no-op, with no warning.

This applies the same interval in the scheduler when `data_parallel_size == 1`. Without
peers there is nothing to align to, so the interval is measured from the last step that
carried prefill rather than against a global grid, which means no shared counter is
needed. Data-parallel deployments are untouched and keep their rank-aligned cadence.

As with the existing DP gate, prefill is deferred only when a running request can decode
in its place (`any(not r.is_prefill_chunk for r in self.running)`), so the interval never
leaves the model idle. The default interval of `1` disables the gate, leaving admission
behavior unchanged.

The motivating deployment is a single engine using decode context parallelism
(`--decode-context-parallel-size 8`). DCP is parallelism *within* one engine, so the
existing DP-only wiring never reaches it, even though the workload benefits from the
cadence as much as a DP deployment does.

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

No open PR touches `prefill_schedule_interval` or `_should_throttle_prefills`. The only
open PR matching `throttle_prefills` is #52969, an unrelated fix for aborted requests.

Two open PRs are adjacent but solve different problems:

- **#49075** (`max_num_partial_prefills` / `max_long_partial_prefills` in V1) bounds *how
  many* prefills run concurrently. This PR controls *how often* a step carries prefill at
  all. The two compose, and neither subsumes the other. Note that #49075 edits both
  scheduling loops, so a textual conflict is possible depending on merge order.
- **#53571** (SLO-aware scheduling policy) reorders the waiting queue by TTFT target,
  changing *which* request is admitted. This PR changes *whether* prefill is admitted on
  a given step, and does not reorder anything.

Checks run (`gh` was not authenticated in my environment, so these were run against the
public search API; the equivalent `gh` invocations are):

```bash
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "prefill gate scheduler"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "throttle_prefills"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "prefill cadence"
```

## Test Plan

Five new tests in `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`, covering the behavior contract:

- `test_local_prefill_interval_holds_prefill_between_bursts[2,4]` — a waiting prefill is
  held for the remainder of the interval while running requests keep decoding, then
  admitted once it elapses.
- `test_local_prefill_interval_defaults_to_no_gating` — the default of 1 admits on the
  next step, i.e. no behavior change.
- `test_local_prefill_interval_left_to_engine_under_dp` — at `data_parallel_size > 1` the
  scheduler does not gate, leaving the rank-aligned cadence to the engine.
- `test_local_prefill_interval_never_idles_the_model` — with nothing running to decode,
  prefill is admitted regardless of the interval.

`create_scheduler` gains a `prefill_schedule_interval` parameter.

## Test Result

All green. Commands and results:

```
pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py                     162 passed  (157 pre-existing + 5 new)
pytest tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py \
       tests/v1/core/test_priority_preemption_bug.py \
       tests/v1/core/test_deferred_block_free.py            30 passed
pytest tests/v1/core/test_priority_scheduler_random.py      12 passed
```

Environment note: the host for these runs has no `torch`, so tests ran inside the
`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` image (vllm `0.28.1rc1.dev108+g1dc464d42`, torch 2.12.0,
Python 3.12) with this checkout's sources overlaid on the installed package, whose build
is a direct ancestor of this branch. This deviates from the `uv`/`.venv` workflow in
`AGENTS.md`; I intend to re-run under the standard workflow before merge.

A single pytest process over all of `tests/v1/core` is SIGKILLed partway through on this
machine, on `main` as well as on this branch, so the suite was run per-file. Each file
passes on its own.

## Serving results

### Kimi-K3

Kimi-K3 FP4, 8x MI355X, a single engine with DCP=8 and LMCache KV offload, replaying an
agentic-coding trace over a 3600s measured window. Interactivity is per-user output speed
at the 90th percentile; higher is better.

The measured configuration enables this PR's `prefill_schedule_interval=33` together with
the cache-aware admission window from #54625 (`--cache-aware-admission-window 64`). The
baseline is the same build with both options absent. The figures below are therefore for
the two options together, not for this change in isolation.

**p90 interactivity (tok/s/user)**

| concurrency | baseline | with both options |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 44 | 11.94 | 17.28 (+44.7%) |
| 48 | 11.32 | 16.33 (+44.3%) |

Interactivity improves by roughly 44% at both concurrencies — the same trade-off the
option already offers under DP, now reachable without it.

Throughput is close to unchanged over the same runs, as expected for a change that
reorders admission rather than removing work: 9,617 to 9,390 tok/s/GPU at concurrency 44
(−2.4%) and 10,537 to 10,103 at concurrency 48 (−4.1%).

An earlier revision of this section reported a `prefill_schedule_interval` sweep at
concurrency 52 against the `vllm-simple` KV offload backend. That backend is no longer
what we run; these numbers replace it.

No accuracy eval was run. Neither the model computation nor sampling is touched; the
change affects only which requests are admitted on a given step. Batch composition does
change, as with any scheduling change, so outputs are not bit-identical. I am happy to
run `tests/evals` or a gsm8k pass if reviewers would like that confirmed.

### Workload shape

Both models replay the same public agentic-coding trace set
(`semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126`): multi-turn tool-calling traffic with
long, highly repetitive contexts. It is worth stating the sequence lengths
explicitly, because they are what makes `prefill_schedule_interval` matter and
they are nothing like a chat workload.

| | MiniMax-M3 agentic | Kimi-K3 agentic |
| --- | --- | --- |
| input length, mean | 104k tokens | 134k tokens |
| input length, p50 / p90 | 77k / 183k | 93k / 266k |
| output length, mean | 687 tokens | 851 tokens |
| output length, p50 / p90 | 288 / 1,524 | 317 / 1,987 |
| input : output ratio | ~151 : 1 | ~158 : 1 |

Requests are prefill-dominated by roughly 150:1 on both models. The practical
consequence: at `--max-num-batched-tokens 32768`, a mean 104k-token prompt is
about 4 prefill chunks and a p90 183k-token prompt about 6, and each chunk
waits for the prefill interval before it can run. The interval is therefore
paid several times per request before that request's first token — which is why
a value tuned on one model should not be assumed to carry over to another with
different prompt lengths.

(Sequence-length distributions only; the two models were measured at different
concurrencies and topologies, so their latency figures are not comparable to
each other.)

### MiniMax-M3

A second model, so the result is not specific to the one MoE the option was
tuned against. MiniMax-M3 MXFP4 on MI355X, **tensor parallel 4**, **prefix
caching enabled**, no KV offload (`offloading=none`), replaying the same
agentic-coding trace set over a 1200s measured window.

Prefix caching being on is load-bearing rather than incidental: #54625 is a
cache-aware admission policy, so with prefix caching disabled there is nothing
for it to be aware of. These runs sustain an 81-90% server-side prefix-cache
hit rate, against a 96.2% theoretical ceiling for this trace set.

**On the absence of KV offloading.** This is a limitation of the MiniMax-M3
numbers rather than a free choice, and it matters for how they are read. The
Kimi-K3 figures above were taken **with** LMCache, and this option is worth
considerably more behind an async KV connector than without one — which is
consistent with the failure mode @hyukjlee described on this PR, where requests
parked in connector lookup make `schedule()` return empty and the pre-fix code
counted those calls against the interval.

We were unable to measure that configuration on MiniMax-M3. With LMCache
enabled, warmup stalls at the same point every time: `num_requests_running=0`
alongside `num_requests_waiting=1`, i.e. a single request parked on the
connector and never admitted, with the GPUs loaded and idle. Two LMCache builds
were tried — `0.5.3` (aborts there) and `0.5.6.dev146+rocm7.2` (hangs there) —
and both the baseline and the treated arm behave identically, so this is not
the scheduler policy. The published MiniMax-M3 agentic CI also runs
`offloading=none` on every job.

So the MiniMax-M3 figures below come from the configuration where this option
has the **least** to offer. They should be read as a lower bound, not as a
like-for-like comparison with the Kimi-K3 numbers.

Server flags follow the published MiniMax-M3 agentic configuration unchanged
(`--enable-chunked-prefill --max-num-batched-tokens 32768`,
`--enable-prefix-caching`, `--max-num-seqs $((2 * CONC))`, fp8 KV cache, EAGLE3
speculative decoding). Both arms run the same image and the same flags; the
only difference is:

```
with both options:  --prefill-schedule-interval 25
                    --cache-aware-admission-window 64
                    --cache-aware-admission-threshold 0
baseline:           neither flag passed
```

Both options default to off, so the baseline is the unpatched behaviour of the
same binary. The flags were read back off each running server to confirm the
only difference is scheduler policy.

**p90 interactivity (tok/s/user)**

| concurrency | baseline | with both options |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 24 | 130.43 | 140.72 (+7.9%) |
| 28 | 143.47 | 165.90 (+15.6%) |
| 32 | 122.37 | 129.15 (+5.5%) |
| 48 | 101.83 | 107.97 (+6.0%) |

Three of the four points sit between +5.5% and +7.9%, with concurrency 28 an
outlier at +15.6%. The effect is therefore consistent rather than
concurrency-dependent over this range.

These figures are not tuned. A single setting --
`prefill_schedule_interval=25`, `cache_aware_admission_window=64` -- was used
at every concurrency; the interval was chosen once from a sweep at concurrency
48, and the window is the value carried over from the Kimi-K3 runs. Neither was
re-tuned per concurrency, and no search was done over the two together. Since
the sweep at a single concurrency already moved p90 interactivity between +1.6%
and +7.3% depending on the interval alone, per-concurrency tuning should be
expected to do better than this. Treat these numbers as a floor for what the
options can deliver on this model, not a ceiling.

Total throughput over the same runs is close to unchanged -- between -3.2% and
-0.1% tok/s/GPU across the four points. That is what this kind of change should do: it
reorders admission rather than removing work.

Concurrencies follow the published agentic configuration for this model,
which validates `conc-list: [32, 48]`.

No accuracy eval was run for this model either, for the same reason as above:
neither model computation nor sampling is touched.

## AI assistance

AI assistance (Cursor) was used to write this change, its tests and this description. I
have reviewed every changed line and can defend the design.

commits.pr_title: [Perf] Fuse the mamba align block-table gather into one Triton kernel, 7 kernels -> 1, 6x speedup on all shapes for this kernel
commits.pr_body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Scope: this is a kernel-level microbenchmark, not an end-to-end throughput claim.**
> The numbers below are measured on the isolated kernel, both versions in the same process. Against a multi-millisecond decode step a
> change of this size sits inside run-to-run variation (~1% on a conc=1 arm), so
> **no measurable serving throughput improvement is claimed, and none should be
> inferred.** The value is removing six of seven kernel launches on a path that is
> on the critical path at low concurrency.

## Purpose

`mamba_get_block_table_tensor`'s `"align"` branch takes the last `1 + num_speculative_blocks` block-table entries of each request:

```python
start_indices = (seq_lens - 1) // kv_cache_spec.block_size
start_indices.clamp_(min=0)
offsets = torch.arange(1 + kv_cache_spec.num_speculative_blocks, ...)
indices_to_gather = (start_indices.unsqueeze(1) + offsets).to(torch.int64)
return torch.gather(block_table, 1, indices_to_gather)
```

The arithmetic is trivial, but as PyTorch ops it is **seven kernel launches** over a `(num_reqs,)` tensor — which holds a **single element** in a one-request decode. Almost all of the cost is launch overhead rather than work.

This is a **shared utility**: `gdn_attn`, `mamba_attn`, `short_conv_attn` and `linear_attn` all call it, so the change is not specific to one model.

## Measured

On MI355X, both versions in the same process so it is like-for-like:

| num_reqs | spec blocks | kernels | us | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **7** | **7 -> 1** | **10.81 -> 1.78** | **6.06x** |
| 1 | 3 | 7 -> 1 | 10.91 -> 1.79 | 6.11x |
| 8 | 7 | 7 -> 1 | 10.73 -> 1.82 | 5.90x |
| 64 | 7 | 7 -> 1 | 12.02 -> 1.95 | 6.16x |

The gain is **flat in batch size**, because the cost is per-launch rather than per-element.

For context on why this site was picked: in a Kimi-K3 concurrency-1 decode trace, attributing every GPU kernel back to its Python call site ranks this the **highest kernels-per-invocation** of any non-model-math site in that model — 7.0 kernels and 19.6 us per invocation. Every other call site in that model is already at or near one kernel per call.

To be explicit about scope: this is a **kernel-level claim**. Against a multi-millisecond decode step it is a fraction of a percent end-to-end, and I am not claiming a measurable throughput change.

## Correctness

**Update after review ([@ChuanLi1101](https://github.com/ChuanLi1101)):** the first version of this kernel indexed the block table as `base + req * stride(0) + start + offs`, which silently assumes a **column stride of 1**. The `torch.gather(block_table, 1, ...)` it replaces honours any layout, and since this is a shared utility a caller holding a non-contiguous view would have read the wrong blocks. The kernel now takes `block_table.stride(0)`, `block_table.stride(1)` and `seq_lens.stride(0)` explicitly, matching the existing `kimi_k3/nvidia/kda_metadata.py` helper.

Worth stating plainly: the original 48-shape sweep below **did not catch this**, because every block table it generated was contiguous. The test added in this PR closes that gap.

Verification now lives in-tree at `tests/v1/attention/test_mamba_align_block_table.py`, so CI runs it rather than it being an out-of-tree script. It pins the kernel to the pre-fusion expression over:

- **48 shape combinations** — `num_reqs` 1/2/8/64 x `block_size` 16/64/256 x `num_speculative_blocks` 0/1/3/7, bit-identical (`atol=0, rtol=0`)
- **a non-contiguous block table** (`stride(1) == 2`) — the regression test for the bug above
- **`seq_len == 0`**, the CUDA-graph padding row the previous `clamp_(min=0)` guarded, which must clamp to row 0
- **`num_reqs == 0`**, which must not launch a `(0,)` grid
- the **`"all"` / `"none"`** passthrough modes, which still return the input tensor itself rather than a copy

55 tests pass against the fixed kernel. The three non-contiguous cases **fail against the previous kernel**, so the suite catches the defect rather than merely covering the line.

The kernel keeps the same in-range assumption the existing `torch.gather` already relies on: `start + num_speculative_blocks` must lie inside the block-table row.

## Test Plan

- [x] `tests/v1/attention/test_mamba_align_block_table.py` — 55 tests, in-tree so CI runs them
- [x] 48 shape combinations bit-identical on device (`atol=0, rtol=0`)
- [x] Non-contiguous block table (`stride(1) != 1`) — fails on the pre-fix kernel, passes now
- [x] Edge cases: `num_reqs == 0`, `seq_len == 0` clamp path, `"all"` / `"none"` passthrough
- [x] Timing on MI355X: 7 kernels -> 1, 10.81 us -> 1.78 us (6.06x) at the single-request shape. **Kernel-level only; no end-to-end throughput claim.**
- [x] `ruff check` / `ruff format` clean

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
